title.zh: 卷一百二十九 列傳第七十九: 韓滉 張延賞
title.en: Volume 129 Biographies 79: Han Huang, Zhang Yanshang
title.raw: 卷一百二十九 列傳第七十九: 韓滉 張延賞 Volume 129 Biographies 79: Han Huang, Zhang Yanshang

sentences.zh: 韓滉，字太沖，太子少師休之子也。

translations.literal: Han Huang, styled Taichong, was a son of Xiu, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, courtesy name Taichong, was the son of Xiu, who had served as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 少貞介好學，以廕解褐左威衛騎曹參軍，出為同官主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he was upright and fond of learning; through yin privilege he entered service as Cavalry Army Adjutant of the Left Weiming Guard, and went out as registrar at Tongguan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was upright and studious; through hereditary privilege he began his career as cavalry adjutant in the Left Weiming Guard and was later posted as registrar at Tongguan.

sentences.zh: 至德初，青齊節度鄧景山辟為判官，授監察御史、兼北海郡司馬，以道路阻絕，因避地山南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era, Deng Jingshan, commissioner of Qing-Qi, recruited him as aide; he was appointed Investigative Censor and concurrently Militia Marshal of Beihai; because roads were blocked, he took refuge in Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era, Deng Jingshan, military governor of Qing and Qi, took him on as aide; he received appointment as investigative censor and concurrent militia marshal of Beihai commandery; when travel routes were cut off, he withdrew to the Shannan region.

sentences.zh: 采訪使李承昭奏充判官，授通州長史、彭王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Investigation Commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized appointing him aide; he was appointed Administrator of Tongzhou and Staff Adviser of the Prince of Peng's household.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized that he serve as aide; he was granted the posts of tongzhou administrator and staff adviser in the Prince of Peng's establishment.

sentences.zh: 鄧景山移鎮淮南，又表為賓佐，未行，除殿中侍御史，追赴京師。

translations.literal: When Deng Jingshan transferred his command to Huainan, he again memorialized for him as staff aide; before he could go, he was appointed Palace Attendant Censor and summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Jingshan moved his headquarters to Huainan, he again nominated Huang as a staff aide; before Huang could take up the post, he was appointed palace attendant censor and ordered to the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，滉兄法知制誥，草王玙拜官之詞，不加虛美，玙頗銜之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huang's elder brother Fa had charge of edict drafting; when drafting Wang Yu's appointment text, he did not add empty flattery, and Yu deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huang's elder brother Fa had been responsible for drafting edicts; when he composed the text appointing Wang Yu, he had not padded it with empty praise, and Yu took strong offense.

sentences.zh: 及其秉政，諸使奏滉兄弟者，必以冗官授之。

translations.literal: When Yu held power, whenever envoys memorialized about the Huang brothers, he always gave them idle appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu was in power, whenever memorials came in concerning the Huang brothers, he always assigned them to nominal posts.

sentences.zh: 玙免相，群議稱其屈，累遷至祠部、孝功、吏部三員外郎。

translations.literal: When Yu left the chancellorship, public comment held that they had been wronged; Huang was successively promoted to external vacancy in the Rites, Filial Achievement, and Personnel ministries.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu was removed from the chancellorship, opinion held that they had been treated unjustly; Huang rose in succession through external vacancies in the ministries of rites, filial achievement, and personnel.

sentences.zh: 滉公潔強直，明於吏道，判南曹凡五年，詳究簿書，無遺纖隱。

translations.literal: In public Huang was upright and strong; he was expert in the arts of office; he judged the Southern Bureau for five years, exhaustively investigating ledgers, with no trace overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: Huang had a reputation for integrity and firmness and was sharp in administrative matters; he handled judgments in the Southern Bureau for five years, scrutinizing registers down to the smallest detail.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，改吏部郎中、給事中。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he was changed to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 時盜殺富平令韋當，縣吏捕獲賊黨，而名隸北軍，監軍魚朝恩以有武材，請詔原其罪，滉密疏駁奏，賊遂伏辜。

translations.literal: At that time bandits killed Wei Dang, magistrate of Fuping; county officers captured the culprits, but their names were listed with the Northern Army; Army Supervisor Yu Chaoen, citing martial ability, requested an edict pardoning their crime; Huang submitted a secret memorial in rebuttal, and the criminals were executed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time robbers killed Wei Dang, magistrate of Fuping county; county clerks seized the gang, but their names were registered with the northern armies; the army supervisor Yu Chaoen, citing their martial talent, asked for an edict to pardon them; Huang sent a confidential memorial arguing against this, and the criminals were put to death.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the right secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，知兵部選。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he took charge of military selections.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took charge of military appointments.

sentences.zh: 六年，改戶部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent commissioner of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became vice minister of revenue and commissioner of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 自至德、乾元已後，所在軍興，賦稅無度，帑藏給納，多務因循。

translations.literal: From the Zhide and Qianyuan eras onward, wherever armies were raised, taxes and levies had no limit; treasury receipts and payments mostly followed old routines.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhide and Qianyuan periods onward, wherever the state raised armies, levies knew no bounds, and treasury intake and disbursement mostly drifted along unchanged.

sentences.zh: 滉既掌司計，清勤檢轄，不容奸妄，下吏及四方行綱過犯者，必痛繩之。

translations.literal: Once Huang held fiscal office, he was diligent and strict in inspection, tolerating no fraud; subordinate clerks and traveling tax officers from all quarters who violated rules were invariably punished severely.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huang controlled the accounts, he worked diligently and audited strictly, brooking no fraud; junior clerks and traveling revenue agents from every circuit who violated regulations were always punished harshly.

sentences.zh: 又屬大曆五年已後，蕃戎罕侵，連歲豐稔，故滉能儲積穀帛，帑藏稍實。

translations.literal: Moreover, after the fifth year of Dali, frontier raids were rare and harvests were abundant year after year; thus Huang was able to store grain and cloth, and the treasury gradually grew solid.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after Dali 5 the frontier was quiet and harvests ran rich for years in a row, so Huang could build up stores of grain and silk and the treasury slowly regained substance.

sentences.zh: 然苛克頗甚，覆治案牘，勾剝深文，人多咨怨。

translations.literal: Yet he was quite harsh and grasping, re-examining case files, pursuing deep legal penalties; many people complained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was harsh to a fault, reopening case files and pressing the law to its extremes, and complaints multiplied.

sentences.zh: 大曆十二年秋，霖雨害稼，京兆尹黎幹奏畿縣損田，滉執雲幹奏不實。

translations.literal: In autumn of the twelfth year of Dali, prolonged rains damaged the crops; Metropolitan Governor Li Gan memorialized damaged fields in the capital districts; Huang held that Gan's report was not true.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Dali 12, rains ruined the harvest; the metropolitan governor Li Gan reported damaged cropland in the capital districts; Huang insisted Gan's figures were false.

sentences.zh: 乃命御史巡覆，回奏諸縣凡損三萬一千一百九十五頃。

translations.literal: He then ordered censors to make another inspection; on returning they reported that in all the counties 31,195 qing of fields had been damaged.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent censors to verify on the ground; they returned reporting that the counties had lost 31,195 qing of fields in all.

sentences.zh: 時渭南令劉藻曲附滉，言所部無損，白於府及戶部。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Zao, magistrate of Weinan, fawned on Huang and said his district had no damage, reporting so to the prefecture and the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The Weinan magistrate Liu Zao curried favor with Huang and claimed his district had suffered no loss, stating this to the prefectural office and the Revenue Ministry.

sentences.zh: 分巡御史趙計復檢行，奏與藻合。

translations.literal: Touring censor Zhao Ji made another inspection and memorialized in agreement with Zao.
translations.idiomatic: The roving censor Zhao Ji reinspected the area and reported in line with Zao.

sentences.zh: 代宗覽奏，以為水旱咸均，不宜渭南獨免，申命御史硃敖再檢，渭南損田三千餘頃。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong read the memorial and thought that in flood and drought all should share alike and Weinan alone should not be exempt; he ordered censor Zhu Ao to inspect again, and Weinan was found with more than 3,000 qing damaged.
translations.idiomatic: The Daizong Emperor reviewed the report and judged that when flood and drought struck, no district should stand alone exempt; he had the censor Zhu Ao inspect again, and Weinan was found to have over 3,000 qing damaged.

sentences.zh: 上謂敖曰：「縣令職在字人，不損猶宜稱損，損而不問，豈有恤隱之意耶！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Ao, "A magistrate's duty is to care for his people; even if there were no damage he should still report damage; if there is damage and he does not inquire—is that the mind of sympathy for the people!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Ao, "A magistrate's charge is to shelter the people; even if there were no loss he ought still to report loss—if damage exists and he stays silent, where is any sympathy for the people?

sentences.zh: 卿之此行，可謂稱職。」

translations.literal: Your journey on this mission may be called fulfilling your duty."
translations.idiomatic: On this mission you have done your office justice."

sentences.zh: 下有司訊鞫，藻、計皆伏罪，藻貶萬州南浦員外尉，計貶豐州員外司戶。

translations.literal: The relevant offices interrogated them; Zao and Ji both confessed guilt; Zao was demoted to external vacancy as wei of Nanpu in Wanzhou, Ji to external vacancy as household registrar in Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices questioned them; Zao and Ji both pleaded guilty; Zao was demoted to external wei at Nanpu in Wanzhou, Ji to external household registrar in Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 滉弄權樹黨，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Huang manipulated power and built factions—all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Huang's abuse of power and faction-building were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 俄改太常卿，議未息，又出為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Director of Rites; criticism had not ceased, and he went out as Prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director of rites; debate had not quieted, and he was posted out as prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 數月，拜蘇州刺史、浙江東西都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed Prefect of Suzhou and commissioner-over-all of the Zhedong circuit for training and observation.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he received appointment as prefect of Suzhou and commissioner-over-all for training and observation in Zhejiang east and west.

sentences.zh: 尋加檢校禮部尚書、兼御史大夫、潤州刺史、鎮軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was further appointed Acting Minister of Rites, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Prefect of Runzhou, and military commissioner of Zhenjun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon additional titles followed: acting minister of rites, concurrent censor-in-chief, prefect of Runzhou, and military commissioner of Zhenjun.

sentences.zh: 滉既移鎮，安輯百姓，均其租稅，未及逾年，境內稱理。

translations.literal: After Huang moved his command, he settled the people and equalized rents and taxes; before a year had passed, the territory was said to be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huang had transferred his headquarters, he pacified the populace and balanced rents and taxes; within a year the circuit was said to be in good order.

sentences.zh: 及建中年冬，涇師之亂，德宗出幸，河、汴騷然，滉訓練士卒，鍛礪戈甲，稱為精勁。

translations.literal: In winter of the Jianzhong year, when the Jingzhou troops revolted, Dezong went out on campaign, the Yellow River region and Bian were in turmoil; Huang trained soldiers and sharpened weapons and armor, which were called elite.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jianzhong, when the troops of Jing rebelled and Dezong fled the capital, the regions of the river and Bian were in uproar; Huang drilled his troops and honed weapons and armor until they were reckoned first-rate.

sentences.zh: 李希烈既陷汴州，滉乃擇其銳卒，令裨將李長榮、王棲曜與宣武軍節度劉玄佐掎角討襲，解寧陵之圍，復宋、汴之路，滉功居多。

translations.literal: After Li Xilie took Bianzhou, Huang selected crack troops and ordered his lieutenants Li Changrong and Wang Qiyao to join forces at an angle with Liu Xuanzuo, military commissioner of Xuanwu, to strike and relieve the siege of Ningling and reopen the roads to Song and Bian; Huang's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xilie seized Bianzhou, Huang chose his best soldiers and had his deputies Li Changrong and Wang Qiyao coordinate with Liu Xuanzuo, military commissioner of Xuanwu, in a pincer attack that lifted the siege of Ningling and reopened the routes to Song and Bian; Huang's share of the credit was largest.

sentences.zh: 然自關中多難，滉即於所部閉關梁，築石頭五城，自京口至玉山，禁馬牛出境；

translations.literal: Yet from the time of many troubles in the Guanzhong, Huang within his territory closed the Liang routes, built five stone fortresses from Jingkou to Yushan, and forbade cattle and horses to leave the border;
translations.idiomatic: But once troubles in the Guanzhong multiplied, he closed the Liang passes within his jurisdiction, raised five stone-walled forts from Jingkou to Yushan, and barred cattle and horses from crossing his borders;

sentences.zh: 造樓船戰艦三十餘艘，以舟師五千人由海門揚威武，至申浦而還；

translations.literal: he built more than thirty decked warships and manned warships, with five thousand naval troops showing might from Haimen, returning when they reached Shenpu;
translations.idiomatic: constructed more than thirty decked war vessels, and sent five thousand sailors under his fleet to display force from Haimen, turning back when they reached Shenpu;

sentences.zh: 毀撤上元縣佛寺道觀四十餘所，修塢壁，建業抵京峴，樓雉相屬，以佛殿材於石頭城繕置館第數十。

translations.literal: he demolished more than forty Buddhist temples and Daoist abbeys in Shangyuan county, repaired ramparts, built watchtowers from Jianye to the Jingxian ridge in continuous line, and used timber from Buddha halls at Stone City to set up several tens of residence compounds.
translations.idiomatic: tore down more than forty Buddhist temples and Daoist shrines in Shangyuan county, repaired walls and towers from Jiankang to the Jingxian ridge in an unbroken line, and used timbers from temple halls at Stone City to erect dozens of mansions.

sentences.zh: 時滉以國家多難，恐有永嘉渡江之事，以為備預，以迎鑾駕，亦申儆自守也。

translations.literal: At that time Huang, because the state was in great difficulty, feared an event like the Yongjia crossing of the Yangzi, made these preparations to meet the imperial carriage, and also showed himself on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Huang thought the realm's troubles might repeat the flight across the Yangzi seen at Yongjia; he framed these measures as readiness to receive the emperor's progress, while also marking his own defences.

sentences.zh: 城中穿深井十丈近百所，下與江平，俾偏將丘涔督其役。

translations.literal: Within the city nearly a hundred wells were dug ten zhang deep, reaching the level of the river; the partial general Qiu Can supervised the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city he sank nearly a hundred wells ten zhang deep down to the river level, with the adjutant Qiu Can supervising the work.

sentences.zh: 涔酷虐士卒，日役千人，朝令夕辦，去城數十里內先賢丘墓，多令毀廢。

translations.literal: Can was brutal to the soldiers; a thousand men a day were mustered with orders due that evening; within several tens of li of the city the tombs of former worthies were largely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Can tormented the troops, pressing a thousand men daily with orders due by nightfall; within tens of li of the city the graves of former worthies were largely torn up.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，追李長榮等戍軍還，以其所親吏盧復為宣州刺史、采石軍使，增營壘，教習長兵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he recalled Li Changrong and other garrison troops, appointed his trusted clerk Lu Fu as Prefect of Xuanzhou and commander of the Shishi army, enlarged camps, and trained long weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he recalled Li Changrong and the frontier garrisons, made his intimate clerk Lu Fu prefect of Xuanzhou and commander at Shishi, expanded fortifications, and drilled long-handled weapons.

sentences.zh: 以佛寺銅鐘鑄弩牙兵器。

translations.literal: He cast crossbow fittings and weapons from bronze bells of Buddhist temples.
translations.idiomatic: Temple bronze bells were melted to cast crossbow fittings and other arms.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊時鎮揚州，以甲士三千人臨江大閱，滉亦以兵三千人臨金山，與少遊相應，樓船於江中，以金銀繒彩互相聘賚。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou then held Yangzhou; with three thousand armored men he reviewed troops along the river; Huang also brought three thousand men to Jinshan in response to Shaoyou; warships stood in the river; gold, silver, and silks were exchanged as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou then governed Yangzhou and paraded three thousand armored men along the Jiang; Huang matched him with three thousand at Jinshan; their warships faced one another mid-river while gold, silver, and silks passed as gifts.

sentences.zh: 而自德宗出居，及歸京師，軍用既繁，道路又阻，關中饑饉，加之以災蝗，江南、兩浙轉輸粟帛，府無虛月，朝廷賴焉。

translations.literal: From the time Dezong left the capital until he returned, military needs were heavy and roads obstructed; Guanzhong suffered famine, compounded by locusts and drought; grain and silk were transported from Jiangnan and the two Zhe circuits so that the treasury was never empty a month—the court relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: From Dezong's flight from the capital until his return, military demands swelled while routes were blocked; Guanzhong starved under drought and locusts; grain and cloth streamed from Jiangnan and the two Zhes so the treasury never went a month bare—the court depended on it.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，就加檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan he was given additional acting Minister of Personnel on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingyuan 1 he received an added acting appointment as minister of personnel in place.

sentences.zh: 數月，又加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Several months later he was further given acting Vice Director of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was further named acting vice director of the right.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年七月，拜檢校左僕射、同平章事，使並如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Zhenyuan 1 he was appointed acting Vice Director of the Left, co-equal chancellor, his envoy powers unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhenyuan 1 he was made acting vice director of the left and associate chief counselor, retaining his commissioner authority.

sentences.zh: 二年春，特封晉國公。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he was specially enfeoffed Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year two he was specially enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，來朝京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year he came to court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That November he came to the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 時右丞元琇判度支，以關輔旱儉，請運江淮租米以給京師。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director Yuan Xie judged the treasury; because the Guanfu region suffered drought and shortage, he requested shipping Jiang-Huai rent grain to supply the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie, vice director, was judging the treasury; with drought and scarcity in the capital districts, he asked to ship Jiang-Huai rent grain to feed the capital.

sentences.zh: 上以滉浙江東西節度，素著威名，加江淮轉運使，欲令專督運務。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Huang as commissioner of Zhedong east and west had long held a formidable name, added him as Jiang-Huai transport commissioner, wishing him to supervise transport affairs exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huang as military governor of eastern and western Zhejiang already bore great authority, the emperor added him transport commissioner for Jiang-Huai, intending that he oversee shipments personally.

sentences.zh: 琇以滉性剛愎，難與集事，乃條奏滉督運江南米至揚子，凡一十八里，揚子以北，皆元琇主之。

translations.literal: Xie, because Huang's nature was obstinate and hard to work with on joint projects, itemized a memorial that Huang should supervise transport of Jiangnan grain only to Yangzi, a distance of eighteen li in all; north of Yangzi, all would be Xie's charge.
translations.idiomatic: Xie found Huang too stubborn for joint work and memorialized in detail: Huang would supervise Jiangnan grain only as far as Yangzi—eighteen li in all—while everything north of Yangzi remained under Xie.

sentences.zh: 滉深怒於琇。

translations.literal: Huang was deeply angry at Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was furious with Xie.

sentences.zh: 琇以京師錢重貨輕，切疾之，乃於江東監院收獲見錢四十餘萬貫，令轉送入關。

translations.literal: Xie, because in the capital money was heavy and goods light, was keenly troubled by this; he collected more than 400,000 strings of current cash at the Jiangdong warehouse and ordered them sent into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xie, troubled that cash weighed heavily against goods in the capital region, collected more than four hundred thousand strings of cash on hand at the Jiangdong depot and ordered them sent inland.

sentences.zh: 滉不許，乃誣奏云：「運千錢至京師，費錢至萬，於國有害。」

translations.literal: Huang did not permit it and falsely memorialized saying, "To transport a thousand cash to the capital costs ten thousand cash—it harms the state."
translations.idiomatic: Huang refused and lodged a false memorial: "Shipping a thousand cash to the capital costs ten thousand in fees—it injures the state."

sentences.zh: 請罷之。

translations.literal: He requested cancellation.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the plan be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 上以問琇，琇奏曰：「一千之重，約與一斗米均。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Xie; Xie memorialized saying, "The weight of a thousand cash is roughly equal to one dou of rice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Xie; Xie replied, "A thousand cash in weight is roughly equal to one dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 自江南水路至京，一千之所運，費三百耳，豈至萬乎？」

translations.literal: From Jiangnan by water route to the capital, what a thousand carries costs only three hundred; how could it reach ten thousand?"
translations.idiomatic: By water from Jiangnan to the capital, carriage for a thousand costs only three hundred—how could it rise to ten thousand?"

sentences.zh: 上然之，遣中使賚手詔令運錢。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and sent a palace envoy bearing a handwritten edict ordering the cash transported.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this and sent a palace envoy with a handwritten edict ordering the money shipped.

sentences.zh: 滉堅執以為不可。

translations.literal: Huang stubbornly held it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Huang still insisted it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，加滉度支諸道轉運鹽鐵等使，遂逞宿怒，累誣奏琇，貶雷州司戶。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year Huang was further given charge as transport commissioner for all circuits, salt, iron, and the like; he then vented old anger and repeatedly falsely memorialized against Xie, who was demoted to household registrar of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That December Huang was further made commissioner for revenue, transport, salt, iron, and the like for all circuits; he then unleashed old resentments, repeatedly denouncing Xie until Xie was demoted to household registrar in Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 其責既重，舉朝以為非罪，多竊議者。

translations.literal: His power was now heavy, and the whole court thought it was not a crime; many privately discussed it.
translations.idiomatic: His authority weighed heavily now; much of the court held that Xie had done no crime, and private talk was widespread.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞董晉謂宰臣劉滋、齊映曰：「元左丞忽有貶責，未知罪名，用刑一濫，誰不危懼？

translations.literal: Vice Director Dong Jin said to the chief counselors Liu Zi and Qi Ying, "Vice Director Yuan has suddenly been demoted and punished; we do not know the crime; once punishment is abused, who will not fear?
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jin, vice director of the left, told the chief counselors Liu Zi and Qi Ying, "Vice Director Yuan has been struck down without our knowing his offence; if penal power runs wild, who will not tremble?

sentences.zh: 假有權臣騁誌，相公何不奏請三司詳斷之。

translations.literal: If some powerful minister indulged his will, would you not memorialized for the three offices to judge in detail?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a powerful minister has had his way—ought you not ask the three offices to adjudicate the case fully?

sentences.zh: 去年關輔用兵，時方蝗旱，琇總國計，夙夜憂勤，以贍給師旅，不增一賦，軍國皆濟，斯可謂之勞臣也。

translations.literal: Last year when troops were used in the Guanfu region, just as locusts and drought struck, Xie oversaw national accounts, worrying day and night, supplying the armies without adding a single levy—the armies and state were both provided for; this may be called a toiling minister.
translations.idiomatic: Last year when Guanfu sent armies, locusts and drought came together; Xie ran the national accounts, laboring day and night, feeding the armies without a single new levy—both armies and state were sustained; that is a minister who has toiled for the realm.

sentences.zh: 今見播逐，恐失人心，人心一搖，則有聞雞起舞者矣。

translations.literal: Now that he is driven out, I fear losing people's hearts; once hearts waver, there will be those who hear the cock and rise to dance.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is cast out, I fear the people's hearts will slip; when hearts waver, someone may yet "hear the cock and rise to dance."

sentences.zh: 竊為相公痛惜之。」

translations.literal: I privately grieve for you, chief counselors."
translations.idiomatic: I grieve for you both in private, gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 滋、映但引過而已。

translations.literal: Zi and Ying only acknowledged fault.
translations.idiomatic: Zi and Ying could only apologize.

sentences.zh: 給事袁高又抗疏申理之，滉誣以朋黨，寢而不行。

translations.literal: Drafting Attendant Yuan Gao also submitted a resistant memorial to argue for him; Huang slandered it as factionalism and the memorial was shelved unexecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting attendant Yuan Gao sent a bold memorial in his defense; Huang smeared it as faction-mongering and the memorial died on the desk.

sentences.zh: 時兩河罷兵，中土寧乂，滉上言：「吐蕃盜有河湟，為日已久。

translations.literal: At that time warfare in the two He regions ceased and the central plains were at peace; Huang memorialized saying, "The Tibetans have long held the theft of He-Huang.
translations.idiomatic: As fighting in the two He regions wound down and the heartland quieted, Huang submitted: "The Tibetans have held the He-Huang region by theft for many years.

sentences.zh: 大曆已前，中國多難，所以肆其侵軼。

translations.literal: Before the Dali era China had many troubles, so they were able to overrun at will.
translations.idiomatic: Before Dali the central state was beset with troubles, which let them raid freely.

sentences.zh: 臣聞其近歲已來，兵眾浸弱，西迫大食之強，北病回紇之眾，東有南詔之防，計其分鎮之外，戰兵在河、隴五六萬而已。

translations.literal: I hear that in recent years their forces have grown weaker: pressed on the west by the might of the Arabs, on the north troubled by the Huige masses, on the east facing Nanzhao's defences; apart from their garrison commands, battle troops in He, Long are only fifty or sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that in recent years their armies have weakened: hard-pressed on the west by the Abbasids, on the north by the Uyghurs, on the east by Nanzhao's defences; outside their scattered commands, fighting men on the He and Long frontier number only fifty or sixty thousand.

sentences.zh: 國家第令三數良將，長驅十萬眾，於涼、鄯、洮、渭並修堅城，各置二萬人，足當守禦之要。

translations.literal: The state need only appoint three or four good generals to drive forward a hundred thousand men, and at Liang, Shan, Tao, Wei jointly repair strong cities, each with twenty thousand men, sufficient for defensive needs.
translations.idiomatic: Let the court assign three or four capable generals to drive a hundred thousand men on a long campaign; strengthen walled cities together at Liang, Shan, Tao, and Wei, twenty thousand men in each—enough to hold the defensive line.

sentences.zh: 臣請以當道所貯蓄財賦為饋運之資，以充三年之費。

translations.literal: I ask to use stored revenues of the circuit in question as supply for transport, sufficient for three years' expense.
translations.idiomatic: I propose funding the campaign from accumulated stores in each circuit, enough to cover three years of costs.

sentences.zh: 然後營田積粟。

translations.literal: Then establish frontier farms and accumulate grain.
translations.idiomatic: Then open military farms and build grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 且耕且戰，收復河、隴二十餘州，可翹足而待也。」

translations.literal: Farming and fighting together, recover more than twenty prefectures of He and Long—it can be awaited with foot raised."
translations.idiomatic: Combine farming with fighting and recover more than twenty prefectures of the He and Long region—success could come within easy reach."

sentences.zh: 上甚納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was much pleased with this advice.

sentences.zh: 滉之入朝也，路由汴州，厚結劉玄佐，將薦其可任邊事，玄佐納其賂，因許之。

translations.literal: When Huang came to court his route passed through Bianzhou; he lavishly cultivated Liu Xuanzuo and was about to recommend him as fit for frontier affairs; Xuanzuo accepted his bribes and therefore promised it.
translations.idiomatic: Huang's road to court ran through Bianzhou, where he lavishly cultivated Liu Xuanzuo and meant to recommend him for frontier command; Xuanzuo took his bribes and promised support.

sentences.zh: 及來覲，上訪問焉，初頗稟命，及滉以疾歸第，玄佐意怠，遂辭邊任，盛陳犬戎未衰，不可輕進。

translations.literal: When he came to audience the emperor inquired; at first he mostly followed his pledge; after Huang withdrew ill to his residence, Xuanzuo's zeal cooled, and he declined frontier appointment, greatly stating that the Rong barbarians were not yet weakened and one must not advance lightly.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor consulted him; at first Xuanzuo largely hewed to his promise; once Huang fell ill and went home, Xuanzuo's zeal cooled and he refused frontier service, insisting loudly that the northern tribes were not yet enfeebled and must not be provoked lightly.

sentences.zh: 滉貞元三年二月，以疾薨，遂寢其事，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the second month of Zhenyuan 3 Huang died of illness at sixty-five, and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhenyuan 3 Huang died of illness at sixty-five, and the campaign plan died with him.

sentences.zh: 上震悼久之，廢朝三日，贈太傅，賻布帛米粟有差。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him long in shock, suspended court three days, posthumously appointed Grand Tutor, and granted condolence gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain in set amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him long in shock, closed court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him grand tutor, and granted condolence gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain according to rank.

sentences.zh: 滉，宰相子，幼有美名，其所結交，皆時之俊彥，非公直者不與之親密。

translations.literal: Huang was a chancellor's son; in youth he had a fine reputation; those he befriended were all eminent men of the time; he was intimate only with those who were upright.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was born to a chancellor's house, won a fine name early, and befriended only the day's best men—he kept close company with those of upright character alone.

sentences.zh: 性持節儉，志在奉公，衣裘茵衽，十年一易，居處陋薄，才蔽風雨。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal and aimed at public service; fur coats and carpet cushions he changed once in ten years; his dwelling was mean, barely sheltering from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: He lived frugally in spirit and cleaved to public duty; furs and cushions he renewed once a decade; his house was mean, barely keeping out wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 弟洄常於裏宅增修廊宇，滉自江南至，即命撤去之，曰：「先公容焉，吾輩奉之，常恐失墜，所有摧圮，葺之則已，豈敢改作，以傷儉德。」

translations.literal: His younger brother Hui often added corridors and halls to the family mansion; when Huang returned from Jiangnan he ordered them torn down, saying, "Our forefather dwelt here; we his descendants keep it in fear of losing it; whatever is broken we repair—how dare we rebuild and wound frugal virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: His brother Hui had enlarged the family compound with new corridors and halls; when Huang came back from the south he had them torn down, saying, "Our father dwelt here—we maintain it in fear of letting it fall; we mend what crumbles—how dare we rebuild and ruin our thrift?"

sentences.zh: 自居重位，愈清儉嫉惡，彌縫闕漏，知無不為，家人盜產，未嘗在意。

translations.literal: Once he held high rank he became still more abstemious and hated corruption, patching every gap, acting wherever he knew—he never cared if the household stole property.
translations.idiomatic: In high office he grew still sterner against waste and graft, plugging every leak and doing all he knew needed doing; he paid no mind when kin pilfered family goods.

sentences.zh: 入仕之初，以至卿相，凡四十年，相繼乘馬五匹，皆及敝帷。

translations.literal: From first entering office to reaching chief minister, forty years in all, he rode five horses in succession, all down to tattered curtains.
translations.idiomatic: From first appointment through chief minister, forty years in all, he used five horses in succession, each worn to tatters.

sentences.zh: 尤工書，兼善丹青，以繪事非急務，自晦其能，未嘗傳之。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at calligraphy and also good at painting; because painting was not urgent business he hid his talent and never passed works around.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at calligraphy and painted well too; because painting was no pressing statecraft he kept that gift hidden and never circulated works.

sentences.zh: 好《易象》及《春秋》，著《春秋通例》及《天文事序議》各一卷。

translations.literal: He loved the Changes and the Spring and Autumn and wrote one scroll each of "General Patterns of the Spring and Autumn" and "Discourse on Astronomical Matters in Order."
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals and wrote one scroll each of General Patterns of the Spring and Autumn and Discourse on the Order of Astronomical Affairs.

sentences.zh: 然以前輩早達，稍薄後進。

translations.literal: Yet because he had risen early as an elder generation, he slightly looked down on juniors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having risen among an older generation, he looked down a little on juniors who came after.

sentences.zh: 晚歲至京師，丞郎卿佐，接之頗倨，眾不能平。

translations.literal: In his last years at the capital he treated vice-directors and aides with considerable arrogance; the crowd could not stomach it.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years at court he treated vice-directors and aides with marked arrogance; colleagues seethed at it.

sentences.zh: 其在浙右也，政令明察，未年傷於嚴急，巡內婺州傍縣有犯其令者，誅及鄰伍，死者數十百人。

translations.literal: In Zheyou his government was clear and sharp; in his last years he harmed people with excessive severity; in a neighboring county of Muzhou within his circuit, those who broke his orders were punished extending to neighboring households; several tens to hundreds died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhe region his rule was lucid and exacting; late on he turned harsh—when a neighboring county in Muzhou broke his orders, punishment spilled into adjoining hamlets and dozens to hundreds died.

sentences.zh: 又俾推覆官分察境內，情涉疑似，必置極法，誅殺殘忍，一判即剿數十人，且無虛日。

translations.literal: He also had investigating officers inspect the territory; where suspicion touched a case, extreme law was applied; killing was cruel—a single judgment might execute several tens, and scarcely a day passed without it.
translations.idiomatic: He set investigating officers across the circuit; wherever suspicion touched a case, the harshest penalty followed; executions ran cruel—one sentence could take dozens of lives, and scarcely a day passed without killings.

sentences.zh: 雖令行禁止，而冤濫相尋。

translations.literal: Although orders were enforced, wrongful slaughter followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Orders were obeyed, but wrongful deaths piled up in their wake.

sentences.zh: 議者以滉統制一方，頗著勤績，自幼立名貞廉，晚途政甚苛慘，身未達則飾情以進，得其志則本質遂彰。

translations.literal: Critics said Huang in governing a region showed considerable merit, from youth established a name for integrity, but in his last years his government was harsh; before he achieved his aims he polished his conduct to advance—once he had his will, his true nature showed.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that Huang's rule of a region showed real merit, that he had been known for integrity since youth, yet that his late rule turned brutal—before he gained his ends he dressed his manner to advance; once he had what he wanted, his true colors showed.

sentences.zh: 子群、臯。

translations.literal: His sons were Qun and Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He left sons Qun and Gao.

sentences.zh: 群，官至考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Qun reached the post of external vacancy in the Ministry of Rites for merit review.
translations.idiomatic: Qun rose to external vacancy in the ministry of rites for merit review.

sentences.zh: 臯字仲聞，夙負令名，而器質重厚，有大臣之度。

translations.literal: Gao, styled Zhongwen, had long borne a fine name, but his substance was weighty and thick, with the breadth of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, courtesy name Zhongwen, had long borne a fine reputation; his character was weighty and measured, with a great minister's breadth.

sentences.zh: 由雲陽尉擢賢良科，拜右拾遺，轉左補闕，累遷起居郎、考功員外郎。

translations.literal: From Cloud-Yang wei he was selected in the eminent talent examination, appointed Right Reminder, transferred Left Collator, and in succession promoted Court Gentleman for Attendance and external vacancy in the Ministry of Rites for merit review.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from Cloud-Yang wei through the eminent-talent examination, he became right reminder, then left collator, rising in turn through attendance gentleman and external vacancy in the ministry of rites for merit review.

sentences.zh: 俄丁父艱，德宗遣中人就第慰問，仍宣令論譔滉之事業，臯號泣承命，立草數千言，德宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his father; Dezong sent a palace envoy to his house to console him and also ordered a discussion drafting Huang's career; Gao wept and accepted the command, immediately drafting several thousand words; Dezong praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he mourned his father; Dezong sent a palace envoy to condole at his home and ordered a discourse on Huang's career; Gao received the command through tears, drafted several thousand words at once, and the emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 及免喪，執政者擬考功郎中，御筆加知制誥。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, the holders of power proposed him for Director of Merit Review; the emperor's brush added control of edict drafting.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, those in power nominated him director in the ministry of merit review; the emperor's own brush added charge of edict drafting.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人、御史中丞、尚書右丞、兵部侍郎，皆稱職。

translations.literal: He was promoted Secretariat Drafter, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Director of the Right, and Vice Minister of War—all were called fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through secretariat drafter, censor-in-chief, vice director of the right, and vice minister of war—at each post he was said to perform well.

sentences.zh: 改京兆尹，奏鄭鋒為倉曹，專掌錢穀。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Metropolitan Prefect, memorialized appointing Zheng Feng as granary clerk, exclusively managing money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed metropolitan prefect and memorialized that Zheng Feng serve as granary clerk with exclusive charge of funds and grain stores.

sentences.zh: 鋒苛刻剝下為事，人皆咨怨。

translations.literal: Feng made harshness and squeezing subordinates his business; people all sighed and resented.
translations.idiomatic: Feng made his business the harsh extortion of subordinates, and everyone groaned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 又勸臯搜索府中雜錢，折糴百姓粟麥等三十萬石進奉，以圖恩寵。

translations.literal: He also urged Gao to search out miscellaneous cash in the prefecture, buying down millet and wheat from the people totaling three hundred thousand shi to present as tribute, to seek imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Gao to scrape together every spare coin in the prefecture, buy up three hundred thousand shi of grain and wheat from the people at depressed prices, and present it as tribute in hopes of winning imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 臯納其計。

translations.literal: Gao accepted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 尋奏鋒為興平縣令。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized appointing Feng as magistrate of Xingping County.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he had Feng promoted to magistrate of Xingping County.

sentences.zh: 及貞元十四年，春夏大旱，粟麥枯槁，畿內百姓，累經臯陳訴，以府中倉庫虛竭，憂迫惶惑，不敢實奏。

translations.literal: When the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan came, spring and summer saw great drought, millet and wheat withered dry; the people within the capital district repeatedly appealed to Gao, but because the prefecture granaries were empty and exhausted, he was anxious, pressed, and fearful, and did not dare report truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, drought in spring and summer shriveled the millet and wheat. The people of the capital district appealed to Gao again and again, but with the prefecture granaries empty he grew anxious and unsettled, and dared not report the situation honestly.

sentences.zh: 會唐安公主女出適右庶子李愬，內官中使於愬家往來，百姓遮道投狀，內官繼以事上聞。

translations.literal: It happened that a daughter of Princess Tang'an was given in marriage to Right Associate of the Heir Apparent Li Su; palace eunuchs and envoys going back and forth at Su's home—the people blocked the road to submit petitions; the eunuchs then reported the matter upward.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that a daughter of Princess Tang'an was marrying Li Su, right associate of the heir apparent. Eunuch envoys were passing in and out of Su's household, and commoners blocked the road to lodge petitions; the eunuchs in turn reported the affair to the throne.

sentences.zh: 德宗下詔曰：「京邑為四方之則，長吏受親人之寄，實系邦本，以分朕憂，茍非其才，是紊於理。

translations.literal: Dezong issued an edict saying: "The capital is the model for the four directions; a chief official receives the charge of caring for the people—it truly ties to the root of the state, to share my cares. If not the right talent, this disorders governance.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong issued an edict: "The capital sets the standard for the realm. Its chief magistrate is entrusted with the welfare of the people and bears on the foundations of the state, sharing my burdens. If he is not equal to the task, governance is thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 正議大夫、守京兆尹、賜紫金魚袋韓臯，比踐清貫，頗聞謹恪，委之尹正，冀效公忠。

translations.literal: Right Grand Master of Remonstrance, acting Metropolitan Prefect, granted purple-gold fish pouch—Han Gao—in recent practice of pure ranks, was much heard to be careful and respectful; entrusting him as prefect, we hoped he would show public loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao—Right Grand Master of Remonstrance, acting metropolitan prefect, granted the purple-gold fish pouch—had lately held office in the purer ranks and was reputed to be diligent and careful. We entrusted him with the capital in the hope he would serve with public loyalty.

sentences.zh: 乃者邦畿之間，粟麥不稔，朕念茲黎庶，方議蠲除，自宜悉心，以副勤恤。

translations.literal: Recently between the capital districts, millet and wheat did not ripen; I think on these common folk, am just discussing remission and reduction—he should have devoted his heart to match diligent care.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the crops have failed in the capital region. Mindful of the people there, I was already considering tax relief—he should have devoted himself wholeheartedly to that humane care.

sentences.zh: 臯奏報失實，處理無方，致令閭井不安，囂然上訴。

translations.literal: Gao's memorial reports were not factual, his handling without method, causing lanes and wells to be unsettled—noisily petitioning upward.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's reports were false, his handling inept, and the neighborhoods grew restless until people cried out in protest to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及令覆視，皆涉虛詞，壅蔽頗深，罔惑斯甚。

translations.literal: When ordered to re-inspect, all involved empty words—obstruction was quite deep, deception and confusion extremely so.
translations.idiomatic: On reinvestigation, everything proved false; the cover-up ran deep, and the deception was egregious.

sentences.zh: 宜加懲誡，以勖守官。

translations.literal: He should receive added punishment and admonition, to encourage those who hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be punished as a warning to officials who hold their posts.

sentences.zh: 可撫州司馬，員外置同正員，馳驛發遣。」。

translations.literal: He may become Secretary at Fuzhou, supernumerary appointment with same rank as regular, dispatched by relay post."
translations.idiomatic: He is demoted to supernumerary secretary at Fuzhou with equal rank to a regular appointee, and dispatched by imperial courier."

sentences.zh: 鋒亦尋出為汀州司馬。

translations.literal: Feng also was soon sent out as Secretary at Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was soon sent out as well, appointed secretary at Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 臯無幾移杭州刺史，復拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Before long Gao was transferred to Prefect of Hangzhou, again appointed Vice Director of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao was transferred to prefect of Hangzhou and again appointed vice director of the right in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 臯恃前輩，頗以簡倨自處。

translations.literal: Gao relied on being senior, and somewhat treated himself with simplicity and arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, counting on his senior standing, carried himself with a certain aloof reserve.

sentences.zh: 順宗時，王叔文黨盛，臯嫉之，謂人曰：「吾不能事新貴。」

translations.literal: During Shunzong's reign, Wang Shuwen's faction flourished; Gao resented them and said to people: "I cannot serve the newly risen elite."
translations.idiomatic: During Shunzong's reign, Wang Shuwen's faction was ascendant. Gao resented them and told others, "I cannot serve these newly risen men."

sentences.zh: 臯從弟曄，幸於叔文，以告之，因出為鄂州刺史、嶽鄂蘄沔等州觀察使。

translations.literal: Gao's younger cousin Ye was favored by Shuwen and told him; therefore Gao was sent out as Prefect of Ezhou and Observation Commissioner of Yue, E, Qi, Mian, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's younger cousin Ye enjoyed Shuwen's favor and reported what Gao had said; Gao was therefore sent out as prefect of Ezhou and observation commissioner over Yue, E, Qi, Mian, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 入為東都留守。

translations.literal: He entered service as Eastern Capital Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as intendant of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 元和八年六月，加檢校吏部尚書，兼許州刺史，充忠武軍節度等使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year of Yuanhe, added Acting Minister of Civil Office, concurrently Prefect of Xuzhou, commissioned as Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army and related duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year of Yuanhe he was given the additional title of acting minister of civil office, made concurrent prefect of Xuzhou, and commissioned military governor of the Zhongwu army and related posts.

sentences.zh: 以陳、許二州水潦之後，賜臯綾絹布葛十萬端疋，以助軍資宴賞。

translations.literal: Because Chen and Xu prefectures had suffered after flooding, Gao was granted one hundred thousand bolts of silk, brocade, cloth, and ramie to aid military funds and feasts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chen and Xu prefectures had been ravaged by flood, Gao was granted one hundred thousand bolts of silk, brocade, cloth, and ramie to support military expenses and feasts and rewards.

sentences.zh: 所理以簡儉稱。

translations.literal: What he governed was praised for simplicity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was praised for its simplicity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，兼太子少傅，判太常卿事。

translations.literal: He entered as Minister of Civil Office, concurrently Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, acting as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as minister of civil office, concurrently junior tutor of the heir apparent, and given charge of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元和十一年三月，皇太后王氏崩，以臯充大明宮使。

translations.literal: Third month of the eleventh year of Yuanhe, Empress Dowager Wang died; Gao was commissioned as Commissioner of Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eleventh year of Yuanhe, Empress Dowager Wang died, and Gao was appointed commissioner of Daming Palace.

sentences.zh: 十五年閏正月，充憲宗山陵禮儀使。

translations.literal: Intercalary first month of the fifteenth year, commissioned as Commissioner for Ceremonial Rites at Xianzong's Imperial Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of the fifteenth year he was appointed commissioner for the ceremonial rites at Xianzong's tomb.

sentences.zh: 三月，穆宗以師保之舊，加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Third month, Muzong, on account of their old tutor relations, added Acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Muzong, remembering their old tutor-student bond, added the title of acting right vice director.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以銓司考科目人失實，與刑部侍郎知選事李建罰一月俸料。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, because the ministry's examination of examination candidates was not factual, he and Vice Minister of Justice Li Jian, who managed selections, were fined one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, because the ministry's review of examination candidates was found to be false, he and Li Jian, vice minister of justice in charge of selections, were fined one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年正月，正拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: First month of the first year of Changqing, formally appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Changqing he was formally appointed right vice director of the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，轉左僕射，赴尚書省上事，命中使宣賜酒饌，及宰臣百僚送上，皆如近式。

translations.literal: Fourth month of the second year, transferred to Left Vice Director, went to the Ministry to assume office; ordered emissaries to announce and grant wine and food, and the chief ministers and all officials to escort him up—all according to recent regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year he was transferred to left vice director, went to the ministry of works to assume office, and was granted wine and a feast by imperial emissary, with chief ministers and the full bureaucracy escorting him—all according to recent custom.

sentences.zh: 其年，以本官東都留守，行及戲源驛暴卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: That year, holding his original rank as Eastern Capital Intendant, while traveling he died suddenly at Xiyuan post station, age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That year, while serving as eastern capital intendant in his existing rank, he died suddenly at Xiyuan post station on the road, at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 大和元年，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dahe, posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dahe he was given the posthumous name Zhen, "Upright."

sentences.zh: 臯生知音律，嘗觀彈琴，至《止息》，嘆曰：「妙哉！

translations.literal: Gao from birth understood pitch and law; once watching someone play the zither, when they reached "Stopping and Resting," he sighed: "Wonderful!
translations.idiomatic: Gao had an innate understanding of pitch and musical law. Once, watching someone play the zither, when the player reached "Stopping and Resting," he sighed, "Marvelous!

sentences.zh: 嵇生之為是曲也，其當晉、魏之際乎！

translations.literal: When Master Ji composed this piece, must it not have been at the juncture of Jin and Wei!
translations.idiomatic: When Master Ji composed this piece, must it not have been at the turning point between Jin and Wei!

sentences.zh: 其音主商，商為秋聲。

translations.literal: Its tone is dominated by shang; shang is the sound of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Its tone is dominated by the shang mode, and shang is the sound of autumn.

sentences.zh: 秋也者，天將搖落肅殺，其歲之晏乎！

translations.literal: Autumn—heaven about to shake down, wither, and kill in severity—is it not the year's decline!
translations.idiomatic: Autumn is when heaven shakes the leaves down in bleak severity—is it not the year's decline!

sentences.zh: 又晉乘金運，商，金聲，此所以知魏之季而晉將代也。

translations.literal: Also Jin rode the fortune of metal; shang is the sound of metal—by this one knows the end of Wei and Jin about to replace it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, moreover, rode the fortune of metal, and shang is the sound of metal—by this one knows that Wei was in its last days and Jin was about to replace it.

sentences.zh: 慢其商弦，與宮同音，是臣奪君之義也，所以知司馬氏之將篡也。

translations.literal: If one loosens its shang strings to match palace in tone, that is the meaning of subject seizing lord—by this one knows the Sima clan was about to usurp.
translations.idiomatic: Loosen the shang strings until they match the palace tone, and that is the image of a subject seizing his lord—by this one knows the Sima clan was about to usurp the throne.

sentences.zh: 司馬懿受魏明帝顧托後嗣，反有篡奪之心，自誅曹爽，逆節彌露。

translations.literal: Sima Yi received Wei Emperor Ming's deathbed charge for the successor, yet harbored usurpation in mind; from killing Cao Shuang, his rebellious intent showed ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi had received Wei Emperor Ming's deathbed charge to protect the successor, yet harbored thoughts of usurpation; from the killing of Cao Shuang onward, his treasonous intent showed ever more plainly.

sentences.zh: 王陵都督揚州，謀立荊王彪；

translations.literal: Wang Ling as governor of Yang province plotted to install Prince Jing Biao;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling, governor of Yang province, plotted to install Prince Jing Biao;

sentences.zh: 毋丘儉、文欽、諸葛誕前後相繼為揚州都督，咸有匡復魏室之謀，皆為懿父子所殺。

translations.literal: Wuqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan in succession governed Yang—each had plans to restore the Wei house—all were killed by Yi and his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan served in succession as governors of Yang province, each with plans to restore the house of Wei, and each was killed by Yi and his sons.

sentences.zh: 叔夜以揚州故廣陵之地，彼四人者，皆魏室文武大臣，咸敗散於廣陵，《散》言魏氏散亡，自廣陵始也。

translations.literal: Jiye took Yangzhou's former Guangling territory—those four men were all Wei civil and military great ministers, all defeated and scattered at Guangling; "Scatter" speaks of Wei's dispersal and ruin, beginning from Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye took Yangzhou's old territory of Guangling—those four men were all great civil and military ministers of Wei, all defeated and scattered at Guangling; "Scatter" means the dispersal and ruin of Wei, beginning at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 《止息》者，晉雖暴興，終止息於此也。

translations.literal: "Stopping and Resting"—though Jin rose violently, it would in the end stop and rest here.
translations.idiomatic: "Stopping and Resting" means that though Jin rose violently, it would in the end come to rest here.

sentences.zh: 其哀憤躁蹙，憯痛迫脅之旨，盡在於是矣。

translations.literal: Its grief, rage, agitation, compression, bitter pain, and forced constraint—all intent is in this.
translations.idiomatic: Its grief, rage, agitation, compression, bitter pain, and sense of forced constraint—all of that intent is contained in this piece.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，其應乎！

translations.literal: The Yongjia disorder—is this its response!
translations.idiomatic: The Yongjia disaster—is this its fulfillment!

sentences.zh: 叔夜撰此，將貽後代之知音者，且避晉、魏之禍，所以托之神鬼也。」

translations.literal: Jiye composed this to bequeath to later generations who understand tone, and also to avoid Jin-Wei disaster—therefore he entrusted it to spirits and ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: Jiye composed this to bequeath it to later generations who would understand, and also to avoid the disasters of Jin and Wei—therefore he entrusted it to spirits and ghosts."

sentences.zh: 洄以廕緒受任，劉晏判鹽鐵度支，辟為屬吏，累官至諫議大夫、知制誥。

translations.literal: Hui received appointment through inherited privilege; Liu Yan as commissioner of salt-iron and revenue recruited him as staff, rising to Remonstrating Adviser and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Hui received office through inherited privilege. Liu Yan, commissioner of salt-iron and revenue, recruited him as a staff officer, and he rose through the ranks to remonstrating adviser and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 與元載善，載誅，以累貶邵州司戶同正員。

translations.literal: Friendly with Yuan Zai; when Zai was executed, he was implicated and demoted to supernumerary Registrar of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Yuan Zai; when Zai was executed, Hui was implicated and demoted to supernumerary registrar of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 建中元年二月，復諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Second month of the first year of Jianzhong, restored as Remonstrating Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Jianzhong he was restored to remonstrating adviser.

sentences.zh: 先以劉晏兼領度支，晏既罷黜，令天下錢穀各歸尚書省。

translations.literal: Previously Liu Yan had concurrently held revenue; once Yan was dismissed, ordered that the empire's money and grain each return to the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan had previously held concurrent charge of revenue; once Yan was dismissed, the court ordered that money and grain affairs throughout the empire revert to the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 本司廢職罷事，久無綱紀，徒收其名而莫綜其任，國用出入，未有所統，故轉洄戶部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: This ministry had abandoned duties and ceased affairs, long without discipline—only collecting the name but not coordinating the charge; state revenue in and out had no unified oversight—therefore Hui was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, acting as Commissioner of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry had long ceased to function in earnest and lacked discipline—it kept the title but did not actually manage the work, and state revenue had no unified oversight—so Hui was transferred to vice minister of revenue with charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 洄上言：「江淮七監，歲鑄錢四萬五千貫，輸於京師，度工用轉送之費，每貫計錢二千，是本倍利也。

translations.literal: Hui submitted: "The seven mints of Jiang-Huai cast forty-five thousand strings of cash per year, delivered to the capital; estimating labor costs and transport fees, each string costs two thousand cash—this is principal doubled in profit.
translations.idiomatic: Hui submitted a memorial: "The seven mints of the Jiang-Huai region cast forty-five thousand strings of cash each year and send them to the capital. Counting labor and transport costs, each string costs two thousand cash—double the principal.

sentences.zh: 今商州有紅崖冶，出銅益多，又有洛源監，久廢不理。

translations.literal: Now Shangzhou has the Hongya smeltery, producing copper in ever greater amounts; there is also the Luoyuan mint, long abandoned and unmanaged.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shangzhou has the Hongya smeltery, which yields ever more copper, and there is also the Luoyuan mint, long abandoned and left unmanaged.

sentences.zh: 請增工鑿山以取銅，興洛源故監，置十爐鑄之。

translations.literal: He requested adding workers to mine mountains for copper, reviving the old Luoyuan mint, setting up ten furnaces to cast it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to add workers to mine the mountains for copper, revive the old Luoyuan mint, and set up ten furnaces to cast coin there.

sentences.zh: 歲計出錢七萬二千貫，度工用轉送之費，貫計錢九百，則利浮本矣。

translations.literal: Per year it would produce seventy-two thousand strings of cash; estimating labor and transport fees, each string would cost nine hundred cash—then profit would exceed principal.
translations.idiomatic: By his estimate the mint would produce seventy-two thousand strings of cash each year; counting labor and transport, each string would cost nine hundred cash—profit would then exceed cost.

sentences.zh: 其江淮七監，請皆罷之。」

translations.literal: As for the seven Jiang-Huai mints, he requested all be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that all seven Jiang-Huai mints be abolished."

sentences.zh: 復以「天下銅鐵之冶，是曰山澤之利，當歸於王者，非諸侯方嶽所有。

translations.literal: He further said: "The empire's copper and iron smelteries are called the profits of mountains and marshes—they should belong to the sovereign, not to regional lords and frontier commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Copper and iron smelteries throughout the empire are profits of the mountains and marshes—they should belong to the sovereign, not to regional lords and frontier commissioners.

sentences.zh: 今諸道節度都團練使皆占之，非宜也，總隸鹽鐵使」。

translations.literal: Now circuit military governors and regimental commissioners all occupy them—this is not fitting; let all be subordinated to the Salt-Iron Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Now the military governors and regimental commissioners of every circuit have seized them, which is improper; let them all be placed under the salt-iron commissioner."

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 洄與楊炎善，炎得罪，常不自安。

translations.literal: Hui was friendly with Yang Yan; when Yan fell from grace, he was often ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was on good terms with Yang Yan; when Yan fell from favor, Hui was often ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 無何，兄子臯抗疏理炎罪，德宗意洄令為之，尋貶蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, his nephew Gao submitted a bold memorial defending Yan's case; Dezong suspected Hui had ordered it, and soon demoted him to Prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his nephew Gao submitted a bold memorial defending Yan; Dezong suspected Hui had put him up to it, and soon demoted Hui to prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 興元元年三月，入為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Third month of the first year of Xingyuan, entered as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Xingyuan he was recalled as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 六月，為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Sixth month, became Metropolitan Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he became metropolitan prefect.

sentences.zh: 七月，加御史大夫。

translations.literal: Seventh month, added Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was given the additional title of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年正月，刑部侍郎劉太真黨於宰相盧杞得罪，以洄代太真為刑部侍郎，尋復兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: First month of the second year of Zhenyuan, Vice Minister of Justice Liu Taizhen, aligned with Chief Minister Lu Qi, fell from grace; Hui replaced Taizhen as Vice Minister of Justice, soon restored as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Zhenyuan, Liu Taizhen, vice minister of justice and ally of chief minister Lu Qi, fell from favor; Hui replaced Taizhen as vice minister of justice and was soon restored to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年十一月，為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Eleventh month of the seventh year of Zhenyuan, became Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the seventh year of Zhenyuan he became chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 張延賞，中書令嘉貞之子。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang was the son of Grand Counselor Jiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang was the son of Grand Counselor Jiazhen.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，本名寶符，開元末，玄宗召見，賜名延賞，取「賞延於世」之義，特授左司禦率府兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, original name Baofu; at the end of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong summoned and saw him, granted the name Yanshang, taking the meaning of "reward extending through generations," specially appointed Left Assistant in the Left Guard Command Military Staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was orphaned in youth; his original name was Baofu. At the end of the Kaiyuan era, Xuanzong summoned him, granted him the name Yanshang—"reward extending through generations"—and specially appointed him assistant in the left guard command military staff.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，達於政事，侍中、韓國公苗晉卿見而奇之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in classics and history, adept at state affairs; Attendant-in-Chief, Duke of Han Miao Jinqing saw him and found him remarkable, giving him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly versed in the classics and histories and skilled in state affairs. Miao Jinqing, attendant-in-chief and duke of Han, saw him and was impressed, and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在鳳翔，擢拜監察御史，賜緋魚袋，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Suzong was at Fengxiang, he was promoted and appointed Investigating Censor, granted the scarlet fish pouch, transferred to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was at Fengxiang, Yanshang was promoted to investigating censor, granted the scarlet fish pouch, and then transferred to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 關內節度使王思禮請為從事，思禮領河東，又為太原少尹，兼行軍司馬、北都副留守。

translations.literal: Guannei Military Governor Wang Sil requested him as staff; when Sil took charge of Hedong, Yanshang also became Vice Prefect of Taiyuan, concurrently Acting Army Marshal and Deputy Intendant of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sil, military governor of Guannei, asked him to serve on his staff; when Sil took charge of Hedong, Yanshang became vice prefect of Taiyuan, concurrently acting army marshal and deputy intendant of the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗幸陜，除給事中，轉御史中丞、中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Daizong visited Shan, appointed Drafting Attendant, transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong visited Shan, Yanshang was appointed drafting attendant, then transferred to vice censor-in-chief and secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年，拜河南尹，充諸道營田副使。

translations.literal: Second year of Dali, appointed Prefect of Henan, commissioned as Deputy Commissioner of Agricultural Colonies for All Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dali he was appointed prefect of Henan and commissioned deputy commissioner of agricultural colonies for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 河洛久當兵沖，閭井丘墟，延賞勤身率下，政尚簡約，疏導河渠，修築宮廟，數年間流庸歸附，邦畿復完，詔書褒美焉。

translations.literal: He-Luo long bore the brunt of armies; lanes and wells were mounds and ruins. Yanshang personally led subordinates with diligence; his government favored simplicity, dredging rivers and canals, repairing palaces and temples—in a few years wandering laborers returned and attached themselves, the capital region was restored whole, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The He-Luo region had long been on the front lines of war; neighborhoods lay in ruins. Yanshang worked diligently and led by example, governing with simplicity, dredging rivers and canals and repairing palaces and temples. Within a few years displaced laborers returned, the capital region was restored, and an edict praised his work.

sentences.zh: 時罷河南、淮西、山南副元帥，以其兵鎮東都，延賞權知東都留守以領之，理行第一，入朝拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the time the deputy marshals of Henan, Huai-Xi, and Shannan were abolished; with their troops garrisoning the eastern capital, Yanshang was temporarily made Eastern Capital Intendant to command them; his governance ranked first, and he entered court worship as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the deputy marshals of Henan, Huai-Xi, and Shannan were abolished and their troops were stationed at the eastern capital, Yanshang was made acting eastern capital intendant to command them. His administration ranked first, and he was recalled to court as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，上封人李少良潛以元載陰事聞，載黨知之，奏少良狂妄，下御史臺訊鞫，欲有所屬。

translations.literal: Earlier, sealed-memorial submitter Li Shaoliang secretly reported Yuan Zai's hidden affairs; Zai's faction learned of it, memorialized that Shaoliang was reckless, sent him down to the Censorate for interrogation, intending to fix blame on someone.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Shaoliang, who had submitted a sealed memorial, secretly reported Yuan Zai's hidden misconduct. Zai's faction learned of it, memorialized that Shaoliang was reckless, and had him interrogated by the censorate, intending to fix blame on someone.

sentences.zh: 延賞不承其意，尋出為揚州刺史、淮南節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: Yanshang did not go along with their intent; soon he was sent out as Prefect of Yangzhou and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang would not go along with their intent and was soon sent out as prefect of Yangzhou and military governor and observation commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 屬歲旱歉，人有亡去他境者，吏或拘之。

translations.literal: It happened to be a year of drought and poor harvest; some people fled to other regions, and officials sometimes detained them.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought drought and poor harvests, and some people fled to other regions; officials sometimes detained them.

sentences.zh: 延賞曰：「夫食，人之所恃而生也，此居而坐斃，適彼而可生，得存吾人，又何限於彼也。」

translations.literal: Yanshang said: "Food is what people rely on to live. Here they sit and die; going there they can live. If we preserve our people, why limit them to that place?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang said, "Food is what people rely on to live. Here they sit and starve; there they may survive. If we can preserve our people, why confine them to this place?"

sentences.zh: 乃具舟楫而遣之，俾吏修其廬室，已其逋債，而歸者增於其舊。

translations.literal: He then provided boats and dispatched them, had officials repair their dwellings, settle their overdue debts, and those who returned increased beyond the old numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He then provided boats and sent them off, had officials repair their homes and settle their overdue debts, and those who returned eventually exceeded the original population.

sentences.zh: 邊江之瓜洲，舟航湊會，而縣屬江南，延賞奏請以江為界，人甚為便。

translations.literal: Guazhou on the river border saw boats and ships gather and meet, but the county belonged to Jiangnan; Yanshang memorialized requesting the river as boundary—people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Guazhou on the river border was a gathering point for shipping, but the county fell under Jiangnan jurisdiction; Yanshang memorialized that the river serve as the boundary, which people found greatly convenient.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職，終制授授檢校禮部尚書、江陵尹、兼御史大夫、荊南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon, on mourning for his mother, he left office; when mourning ended, appointed Acting Minister of Rites, Prefect of Jiangling, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office to mourn his mother; when mourning ended he was appointed acting minister of rites, prefect of Jiangling, concurrently censor-in-chief and military governor and observation commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 數年，改檢校兵部尚書、成都尹、劍南西川節度觀察使，依前兼御史大夫，尋就加吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After several years, changed to Acting Minister of War, Prefect of Chengdu, Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit, as before concurrently Censor-in-Chief; soon added Minister of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was transferred to acting minister of war, prefect of Chengdu, and military governor and observation commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit, still concurrently censor-in-chief; soon afterward he was further given the title minister of civil office.

sentences.zh: 建中四年十一月，部將西山兵馬使張朏以兵入成都為亂，延賞奔漢州鹿頭，戍將叱幹遂等討之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month of the fourth year of Jianzhong, subordinate general Zhang Fei of the Xishan army entered Chengdu with troops in rebellion; Yanshang fled to Lutou in Hanzhou; garrison generals Chigan Sui and others suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Jianzhong, Zhang Fei, a subordinate general of the Xishan army, entered Chengdu with troops and raised a rebellion. Yanshang fled to Lutou in Hanzhou, and garrison generals including Chigan Sui put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 其月，斬朏及同惡者，復歸成都。

translations.literal: That month, Fei and fellow evildoers were beheaded; Yanshang returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Fei and his accomplices were executed, and Yanshang returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 先是兵革屢擾，自天寶末楊國忠用事南蠻，三蜀疲弊，屬車駕遷幸；

translations.literal: Earlier armies and warfare had repeatedly disturbed the region; from the end of Tianbao, when Yang Guozhong wielded power over the southern barbarians, the Three Shu were exhausted and depleted, and then the imperial carriage moved in flight;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the region had been repeatedly ravaged by war. From the end of the Tianbao era, when Yang Guozhong wielded power over the southern frontier, the Three Shu were exhausted and depleted, and then the court fled the capital;

sentences.zh: 其後郭英乂淫崔寧之室，遂縱崔寧、楊琳交亂；

translations.literal: Afterward Guo Yingyi violated Cui Ning's wife, then indulged Cui Ning and Yang Lin in mutual disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Guo Yingyi violated Cui Ning's wife, then allowed Cui Ning and Yang Lin to plunge the region into mutual disorder;

sentences.zh: 及崔寧得志，復極侈靡，故蜀土殘弊，蕩然無制度。

translations.literal: When Cui Ning got his way, he again was extremely extravagant; therefore Shu lands were ruined and depleted, swept bare of all institutions.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Ning gained power he again lived in extreme extravagance, so the land of Shu was left ruined and depleted, with institutions swept away entirely.

sentences.zh: 延賞薄賦約事，動遵法度，僅至庶富焉。

translations.literal: Yanshang kept taxes light and affairs restrained, always following law and regulation, barely reaching common prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang kept taxes light and administration restrained, always following the law, and brought the region to a modest prosperity.

sentences.zh: 建中末，駕在山南，延賞貢奉供億，頗竭忠力焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong, the carriage was in Shannan; Yanshang presented tribute and supplies, quite exhausting loyal effort.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianzhong era, when the emperor was in Shannan, Yanshang sent tribute and supplies and exerted himself loyally on the court's behalf.

sentences.zh: 駕在梁州，倚劍南蜀川為根本。

translations.literal: When the carriage was at Liangzhou, it relied on Jiannan and Shu as foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Liangzhou, the court relied on Jiannan and Shu as its foundation.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，以宰相劉從一有疾，詔征延賞為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: First year of Zhenyuan, because Chief Minister Liu Congyi was ill, an edict summoned Yanshang as Vice Grand Counselor, Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan, because chief minister Liu Congyi was ill, an edict summoned Yanshang to serve as vice grand counselor and associate director of the secretariat-chancellery.

sentences.zh: 與鳳翔節度使李晟不協，晟表論延賞過惡，德宗重違晟意，延賞至興元，改授左僕射。

translations.literal: He did not get along with Fengxiang Military Governor Li Sheng; Sheng memorialized discussing Yanshang's faults and evils; Dezong heavily weighed going against Sheng's intent—when Yanshang reached Xingyuan, he was reassigned Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He did not get along with Li Sheng, military governor of Fengxiang. Sheng memorialized listing Yanshang's faults, and Dezong, reluctant to go against Sheng, reassigned Yanshang to left vice director when he reached Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，大曆末，吐蕃寇劍南，李晟領神策軍戍之，及旋師，以成都官妓高氏歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Dali, Tibetans raided Jiannan; Li Sheng led the Shence Army to garrison there, and when the army returned, he took the Chengdu courtesan Lady Gao home with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of the Dali era, Tibetans raided Jiannan. Li Sheng led the Shence Army to garrison the region, and when the army withdrew he brought home Lady Gao, a Chengdu courtesan.

sentences.zh: 延賞聞而大怒，即使將吏令追還焉。

translations.literal: Yanshang heard and was greatly angered, immediately sent generals and officials ordering her returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang was furious when he heard of it and immediately sent officers to order her returned.

sentences.zh: 晟頗銜之，形於詞色。

translations.literal: Sheng quite harbored resentment, showing it in words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng deeply resented this and showed it plainly in word and manner.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，晟入朝，詔晟與延賞釋憾，德宗註意於延賞，將用之。

translations.literal: Third year, first month, Sheng entered court; an edict ordered Sheng and Yanshang to release resentment; Dezong fixed attention on Yanshang, intending to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Sheng came to court. An edict ordered Sheng and Yanshang to set aside their grievances. Dezong had his eye on Yanshang and intended to use him.

sentences.zh: 會浙西觀察使韓滉來朝，嘗有德於晟，因會宴說晟使釋憾，遂同飲極歡，且請晟表薦為相，晟然之，於是復加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhexi Observation Commissioner Han Huang came to court—he had once shown kindness to Sheng—so at a banquet he persuaded Sheng to release resentment; they then drank together in great joy, and Huang asked Sheng to memorial-recommend [Yanshang] as chief minister; Sheng agreed; therefore Yanshang was again added Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Han Huang, observation commissioner of Zhexi, came to court. Huang had once done Sheng a kindness, and at a banquet he persuaded Sheng to set aside his grievance with Yanshang. They drank together in great harmony, and Huang asked Sheng to recommend Yanshang for chief minister in a memorial. Sheng agreed, and Yanshang was again appointed associate director of the secretariat-chancellery.

sentences.zh: 及延賞當國用事，晟請一子聘其女，固情好焉，延賞拒而不許。

translations.literal: When Yanshang came to power and held sway over state affairs, Sheng asked that one of his sons be betrothed to Yanshang's daughter to cement friendship between them, but Yanshang refused and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanshang gained control of the government, Sheng asked to betroth one of his sons to Yanshang's daughter, intending to firm up their friendship. Yanshang refused.

sentences.zh: 晟謂人曰：「武人性快，若釋舊惡於杯酒之間，終歡可解。

translations.literal: Sheng said to people: "Military men are quick-tempered; if old enmity is released over cups of wine, ultimate harmony can resolve it.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng told others, "Soldiers are quick-tempered. If old grudges can be cleared over a few cups of wine, enmity can always be put to rest.

sentences.zh: 文士難犯，雖修睦於外，而蓄怒於內，今不許婚，釁未忘也，得無懼焉！」
