translations.literal: Literary men are hard to offend outwardly—though they cultivate amity on the surface, they hoard anger within. Now he does not consent to the marriage; the feud is not forgotten—is there not cause to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Scholars are another matter. They may act friendly on the surface while nursing anger inside. He has refused the marriage match, so the quarrel is clearly not forgotten. Should I not be afraid?

sentences.zh: 無幾，延賞果謀罷晟兵權。

translations.literal: Not long after, Yanshang indeed plotted to strip Sheng of his military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Yanshang did in fact move to strip Sheng of his military command.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃尚結贊興兵入隴州，抵鳳翔，無所虜掠，且曰：「召我來，何不持牛酒勞軍？」

translations.literal: At first, the Tubo general Shang Jiezan raised troops and entered Long Prefecture, reaching Fengxiang. They carried off nothing by plunder, and moreover said: "You summoned us—why not bring cattle and wine to reward the army?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Tibetan commander Shang Jiezan had marched into Long Prefecture and reached Fengxiang without looting anything, saying, "You summoned us here—why have you not brought cattle and wine to reward our troops?

sentences.zh: 徐乃引去，持是以間晟。

translations.literal: Then slowly they withdrew. Yanshang used this matter to slander Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Then they withdrew at leisure, and Yanshang used the incident to sow discord against Sheng.

sentences.zh: 晟令牙將王佖選銳兵三千設伏汧陽，大敗吐蕃，結贊僅免，自是數遣使乞和。

translations.literal: Sheng ordered staff general Wang Ji to select three thousand elite troops and set an ambush at Qianyang; they greatly defeated the Tubo, Jiezan barely escaped, and from this time sent envoys repeatedly begging for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ordered his staff general Wang Ji to choose three thousand crack troops and lay an ambush at Qianyang. The Tang forces routed the Tibetans; Jiezan barely escaped. After that the Tibetans repeatedly sent envoys suing for peace.

sentences.zh: 晟朝於京師，奏曰：「戎狄無信，不可許。」

translations.literal: Sheng attended court at the capital and memorialized: "The Rong and Di are faithless—peace cannot be granted."
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng came to court in the capital, he memorialized, "The barbarians are untrustworthy. We must not agree to peace.

sentences.zh: 宰相韓滉又扶晟議，請調軍食以繼之，上意將帥生事邀功。

translations.literal: Chief minister Han Huang again supported Sheng's view, asking to transfer army provisions to supply him. The emperor suspected that the military commanders were creating incidents to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Han Huang again backed Sheng's position and asked that army provisions be sent to support him. The emperor, however, suspected that his generals were manufacturing trouble to win credit for themselves.

sentences.zh: 會滉卒，延賞揣上意，遂行其志，奏令給事中鄭雲逵代之。

translations.literal: It happened that Huang died. Yanshang gauged the emperor's intent and so carried out his plan, memorializing that Supervising Secretary Zheng Yunkui replace Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang died, Yanshang read the emperor's mind and got his way, memorializing that Supervising Secretary Zheng Yunkui replace Sheng.

sentences.zh: 上不許，且曰：「晟有社稷之功，令自舉代己者。」

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent, and moreover said: "Sheng has merit to the altars of state—let him himself recommend one to replace him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and said, "Sheng has rendered great service to the dynasty. Let him nominate his own replacement.

sentences.zh: 於是始用邢君牙焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they first employed Xing Junya.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Junya was then appointed.

sentences.zh: 拜晟太尉、兼中書令，奉朝請而已。

translations.literal: Sheng was appointed Grand Tutor and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, attending court only.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was given the titles of Grand Tutor and concurrent director of the secretariat, with ceremonial attendance at court but no real power.

sentences.zh: 是年五月，吐蕃果背約以劫渾瑊。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month, the Tubo indeed broke the treaty and attacked Hun Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: That May the Tibetans broke their pact as Sheng had predicted and raided Hun Zhen.

sentences.zh: 及冊晟太尉，故事，臨軒冊拜三公，中書令讀冊，侍中奉禮，如闕，即以宰相攝之。

translations.literal: When Sheng was enfeoffed as Grand Tutor, by precedent when holding a ceremony at the imperial porch to invest the Three Dukes, the Director of the Secretariat reads the patent; the Palace Attendant presents the ritual vessels—if either post is vacant, a chief minister acts in that capacity.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng was invested as Grand Tutor, precedent held that the director of the secretariat should read the patent and the palace attendant perform the ritual at the imperial porch. If either office was vacant, a chief minister would stand in.

sentences.zh: 延賞欲輕其禮，始令兵部尚書崔漢衡攝中書令讀冊，時議非之。

translations.literal: Yanshang wished to lighten the ceremony and first ordered Minister of War Cui Hanheng to act as Director of the Secretariat and read the patent; contemporary opinion criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang wanted to slight the ceremony and had Minister of War Cui Hanheng read the patent as acting director of the secretariat, which contemporaries condemned.

sentences.zh: 延賞奏議請省官員，曰：「為政之本，必先命官。

translations.literal: Yanshang submitted a memorial petitioning to reduce official posts, saying: "The root of governing lies first in appointing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang submitted a memorial proposing to cut the official roster, arguing, "The foundation of government is appointing officials in the first place.

sentences.zh: 舊制官員繁而且費，州縣殘破，職此之由。

translations.literal: The old system had officials numerous and costly; prefectures and counties lay in ruin—this was the cause of it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system posts had proliferated and grown costly, and it was for this reason that prefectures and counties had fallen into ruin.

sentences.zh: 臣在荊南、劍南，所管州縣闕官員者，少不下十數年，吏部未嘗補授，但令一官假攝，公事亦理。

translations.literal: When I was in Jingnan and Jiannan, among the prefectures and counties under my jurisdiction those lacking officials went without them for no less than ten-odd years; the Ministry of Personnel never once filled appointments—only one official was ordered to act temporarily, and public business was still managed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingnan and Jiannan, which I administered, some counties and prefectures had gone without appointed officials for ten years or more. The Ministry of Personnel never filled the posts; a single acting official was enough to keep affairs in order.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，員可減無疑也。

translations.literal: From this speaking, the number of posts can be reduced without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That proves beyond doubt that the roster can be trimmed.

sentences.zh: 請減官員，收其祿俸，資幕職戰士，俾劉玄佐復河湟，軍用不乏矣。」

translations.literal: I ask to reduce officials, collect their salaries, and fund staff-duty warriors, enabling Liu Xuanzuo to recover the He-Huang region—military supplies would not lack."
translations.idiomatic: I propose cutting posts, redirecting the salaries saved to support military staff, and enabling Liu Xuanzuo to recover the He-Huang region, so that military supplies will not run short.

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，韓滉入朝，至汴州，厚結劉玄佐，將薦其可委邊任，玄佐亦欲自效，初稟命，及滉卒，玄佐以疾辭，上遣中官勞問，臥以受命。

translations.literal: At first, when Han Huang entered court, reaching Bian Prefecture he formed close ties with Liu Xuanzuo and was about to recommend him as one who could be entrusted with border duty; Xuanzuo also wished to prove his worth and initially received the order. When Huang died, Xuanzuo declined on grounds of illness; the emperor sent a palace eunuch to condole and inquire—he received the order while lying sick.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Huang came to court he stopped at Bian Prefecture and cultivated a close tie with Liu Xuanzuo, intending to recommend him for a frontier command. Xuanzuo was willing to serve and had initially accepted the appointment. After Huang died, Xuanzuo pleaded illness to decline. The emperor sent a palace eunuch to console him, and he accepted the commission while still abed.

sentences.zh: 延賞知不可用，奏用李抱真，抱真亦辭不行。

translations.literal: Yanshang knew Xuanzuo could not be used and memorialized to employ Li Baozhen; Baozhen also declined and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang saw that Xuanzuo could not be relied on and memorialized to appoint Li Baozhen instead, but Baozhen too refused to take the post.

sentences.zh: 時抱真判官陳曇奏事京師，延賞俾曇勸抱真，竟拒絕之。

translations.literal: At the time Baozhen's aide Chen Tan was in the capital on official business; Yanshang had Tan persuade Baozhen—he ultimately refused.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen's aide Chen Tan was then in the capital on official business; Yanshang had Tan urge Baozhen to accept, but Baozhen still refused.

sentences.zh: 蓋以延賞挾怨罷李晟兵柄，由是武臣不附。

translations.literal: This was because Yanshang, bearing a grudge, had stripped Li Sheng of military command—therefore military men did not attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yanshang had used a personal grudge to strip Li Sheng of command, the military men would not rally to him.

sentences.zh: 自建議減員之後，物議不平。

translations.literal: From the time he built the proposal to reduce posts, public opinion was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion turned against him after his proposal to cut posts.

sentences.zh: 延賞懼，量留其官，下詔曰：「諸州府停減及所留官，並合厘務。

translations.literal: Yanshang feared this; he selectively retained some posts and issued an edict saying: "Officials in various prefectures whose posts were halted or reduced, and those retained, should all attend to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Yanshang partially walked back the cuts and issued an edict: "Officials whose posts were abolished or retained in the various prefectures must all fulfill their duties.

sentences.zh: 其中有先考滿及充職掌，遇停減或恐公務有闕，宜委長吏於合停官中取考淺人清白幹舉者，留填闕官，差攝訖聞奏。

translations.literal: Among them there are those who completed their service evaluation and filled official responsibilities; encountering post reduction, lest public business have gaps, the senior official should be delegated to select from those whose posts ought to be halted persons of shallow seniority who are upright and capable, retain them to fill vacant posts, assign them to act provisionally, and upon completion report by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Where abolitions might leave gaps in official business, senior officials should select capable, upright men of lesser seniority from among those slated for removal to fill vacant posts on a provisional basis and report when done.

sentences.zh: 但取才堪，不限資序。

translations.literal: Only talent and fitness are to be taken—not limited by qualifications and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Merit alone should govern the choice, not rank or seniority.

sentences.zh: 如當州官少，任以鄰州官充。

translations.literal: If officials in that prefecture are few, officials from neighboring prefectures may serve in their place.
translations.idiomatic: If a prefecture has too few officials, men from neighboring prefectures may be assigned.

sentences.zh: 其州縣諸色部送，準舊例以當州官及本土寄客有資產幹了者差遣。」

translations.literal: As for the various categories of departmental relay service in prefectures and counties, according to old precedent officials of the prefecture and locally resident sojourners with assets and capable management shall be dispatched."
translations.idiomatic: For the various relay and transport duties at the prefectural and county level, the old practice of assigning local officials or resident merchants of means and ability should be followed.

sentences.zh: 及減員人眾，道路怨嘆，日聞於上。

translations.literal: When those whose posts were reduced became numerous, complaints and laments on the roads daily reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced officials filled the roads with complaints that soon reached the emperor daily.

sentences.zh: 侍中馬燧奏減員太甚，恐不可行；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Ma Sui memorialized that the reduction of posts was too extreme and feared it could not be carried out;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Ma Sui argued that the cuts had gone too far and would not work;

sentences.zh: 太子少保韋倫及常參官等各抗疏以減員招怨，並請復之；

translations.literal: Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Wei Lun and regular attendees at court each submitted memorials opposing the post reduction as inviting resentment, and all asked to restore them;
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Wei Lun and other regular attendees at court all submitted opposing memorials warning that the cuts were stirring resentment, and asked that the posts be restored;

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使白誌貞亦以疏論。

translations.literal: Zhexi Observation Commissioner Bai Zhizhen also submitted a memorial on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zhizhen, observation commissioner of Zhexi, also weighed in by memorial.

sentences.zh: 時廷賞疾甚，在私第；

translations.literal: At the time Yanshang was gravely ill and in his private residence;
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang was by then seriously ill and confined to his private residence;

sentences.zh: 李泌初為相，采於群情，由是官員悉復。

translations.literal: Li Bi, newly made chief minister, took the pulse of popular sentiment—whereupon all official posts were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi had just become chief minister. Reading the mood of the court, he restored all the abolished posts.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年七月薨，年六十一，廢朝三日，贈太保，賻禮加等，謚曰成肅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Zhenyuan year 3 he died, age sixty-one; court was suspended three days; posthumously honored as Grand Guardian; funeral gifts graded higher; posthumous title Chengsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of Zhenyuan 3, at the age of sixty-one. Court mourning was observed for three days. He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian, his funeral gifts were increased by one grade, and he was given the posthumous title Chengsu.

sentences.zh: 子弘靖，字元理，雅厚信直。

translations.literal: His son Hongjing, styled Yuanli, was refined, generous, trustworthy, and upright.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjing, courtesy name Yuanli, was refined, generous, trustworthy, and upright.

sentences.zh: 少以門廕授河南府參軍，調補藍田尉。

translations.literal: In youth through hereditary privilege he was appointed army adjutant of Henan Prefecture; transferred to fill the post of captain at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he began as an aide in Henan Prefecture and was later transferred to captain of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 東都留守杜亞辟為從事，奏改監察御史裏行，轉殿中侍御史、內供奉。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital intendant Du Ya recruited him as aide; memorialized to change his post to probationary investigative censor; transferred to palace censor and inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya, intendant of the Eastern Capital, took him on as a staff aide and had him appointed probationary investigative censor, then transferred him to palace censor with inner-attendant status.

sentences.zh: 留守將令狐運逐賊出郊，其日有劫轉運絹於道者，亞以運豪家子，意其為之，乃令判官穆員及弘靖同鞫其事。

translations.literal: The intendant's general Linghu Yun drove bandits out to the suburbs; that day silk for transport relay was robbed on the road. Ya, because Yun was the son of a powerful family, suspected he had done it; he therefore ordered aide Mu Yuan and Hongjing jointly to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When intendant general Linghu Yun drove bandits beyond the suburbs, transport silk was robbed on the road that same day. Du Ya, believing that Yun, as the son of a powerful family, was responsible, ordered his aides Mu Yuan and Hongjing to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 員與弘靖皆以運職在牙門，必不為盜，堅請不按。

translations.literal: Yuan and Hongjing both believed that since Yun's duty was at the headquarters gate, he would not be a robber—they firmly pleaded not to pursue the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Hongjing argued that Yun's post at headquarters made it impossible he had committed the robbery, and they firmly refused to proceed with the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 亞不聽，遂以獄聞，仍斥員及弘靖出幕府，有詔令三司使雜治之，後果於河南界得賊。

translations.literal: Ya would not listen; he reported the legal case upward, and furthermore expelled Yuan and Hongjing from the staff office. An edict ordered the Three Offices to jointly try the matter; afterward the bandits were indeed captured at the Henan border.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya ignored them, reported the case to the throne, and expelled Yuan and Hongjing from his staff. An edict ordered a joint trial by the Three Offices; the real robbers were later caught on the Henan border.

sentences.zh: 無何，德陽公主下嫁，治第將侵弘靖家廟。

translations.literal: Before long, Princess Deyang descended in marriage; construction of her residence was about to encroach on Hongjing's family ancestral shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, when Princess Deyang was given in marriage, work on her new residence threatened to encroach on the Hong family ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 弘靖拜表陳情，具述祖考之德，德宗慰撫之，不令毀廟。

translations.literal: Hongjing submitted a memorial stating his feelings and fully recounting the virtues of his ancestors; Dezong consoled and reassured him and did not allow the shrine to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing submitted a memorial pleading his case and recounting his ancestors' virtues. Emperor Dezong consoled him and forbade the destruction of the shrine.

sentences.zh: 又獻賦美二京之制，德宗嘉其文，擢授監察御史。

translations.literal: He also presented a rhapsody praising the institutions of the Two Capitals; Dezong admired his writing and promoted him to investigative censor.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a rhapsody praising the institutions of the Two Capitals. Dezong admired the piece and promoted him to investigative censor.

sentences.zh: 轉殿中侍御史、禮部員外郎；

translations.literal: Transferred to palace censor and deputy director in the Ministry of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace censor and then deputy director in the Ministry of Rites;

sentences.zh: 遷兵部郎中、知制誥、中書舍人、知東都選事；

translations.literal: Promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of War, drafting edicts, Secretariat drafter, in charge of Eastern Capital selection matters;
translations.idiomatic: he rose to bureau director in the Ministry of War, took charge of drafting edicts, became a secretariat drafter, and oversaw civil-service selection in the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 拜工部侍郎，轉戶部侍郎、陜州觀察、河中節度使；

translations.literal: Appointed vice minister of works; transferred to vice minister of revenue, Shaan Prefecture observation commissioner, Hezhong military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: he was appointed vice minister of works, then vice minister of revenue, observation commissioner of Shaan Prefecture, and military governor of Hezhong;

sentences.zh: 拜刑部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Appointed minister of justice and associate director of the secretariat-chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: and finally minister of justice and associate director of the secretariat-chancellery.

sentences.zh: 吳少陽死，其子元濟擅主留務，憲宗怒，欲下詔誅之。

translations.literal: Wu Shaoyang died; his son Yuanji usurped control of the acting command; Xianzong was angry and wished to issue an edict condemning him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shaoyang died, his son Yuanji seized control of the garrison affairs. Emperor Xianzong was furious and wanted to issue an edict calling for his execution.

sentences.zh: 弘靖請先命吊贈使，待其不恭，然後加兵，憲宗從其議。

translations.literal: Hongjing asked first to dispatch a condolence-and-grant envoy; wait until he showed disrespect, then add troops. Xianzong followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing advised sending a condolence envoy first and waiting until Yuanji showed disrespect before committing troops. Xianzong accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 尋加中書侍郎平章事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was additionally made Vice Director of the Secretariat and chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further appointed vice director of the secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 盜殺宰相武光衡，京師索賊未得。

translations.literal: Robbers killed chief minister Wu Yuanheng; the capital searched for the culprits without success.
translations.idiomatic: Assassins killed Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng, and the capital's search for the killers came up empty.

sentences.zh: 時王承宗邸中有鎮卒張晏輩數人，行止無狀，人多意之，詔錄付御史陳中師按之，皆附致其罪，如京中所說。

translations.literal: At the time in Wang Chengzong's residence there were several garrison soldiers such as Zhang Yan whose conduct was suspicious; many people suspected them. An edict ordered them arrested and handed to censor Chen Zhongshi to investigate—all were implicated in the crime, as rumormongers in the capital had said.
translations.idiomatic: Several garrison soldiers under Wang Chengzong's household, including a man named Zhang Yan, had been acting suspiciously, and many suspected them. An edict ordered their arrest and investigation by Censor Chen Zhongshi, who implicated them all exactly as rumor in the capital had it.

sentences.zh: 弘靖疑其不直，驟於上前言之，憲宗不聽，竟殺張晏輩。

translations.literal: Hongjing suspected the case was not straight and suddenly spoke of it before the emperor; Xianzong did not listen and in the end executed Zhang Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing doubted the case was sound and abruptly raised the matter before the emperor. Xianzong refused to listen, and Zhang Yan and the others were executed.

sentences.zh: 及田弘正入鄆，按簿書，亦有殺元衡者，但事暖味，互有所說，卒未得其實。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng entered Yun, examining the records, there were also references to those who killed Yuanheng, but the matter was obscure and conflicting accounts were given—they ultimately did not obtain the truth.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng later entered Yun and examined the records, he also found references to Yuanheng's killers, but the matter remained murky and the accounts conflicted; the truth was never established.

sentences.zh: 又殺張晏後，憲宗欲遂伐承宗。

translations.literal: Moreover, after executing Zhang Yan, Xianzong wished immediately to campaign against Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yan's execution, Xianzong wanted to march immediately against Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 弘靖以為戎事並興，鮮有濟者，不如併攻元濟，待淮西平，然後悉師河朔。

translations.literal: Hongjing believed that if military affairs were launched together, few would succeed; better to combine forces against Yuanji—wait until Huai West was pacified, then commit all troops to the Hebei region.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing argued that fighting on two fronts rarely succeeded. Better to concentrate on Yuanji, wait until Huaixi was pacified, and then commit the full army to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 憲宗業已北討，不為之止，然亦重違其言。

translations.literal: Xianzong had already begun the northern campaign and did not stop it for this, yet he also attached great weight to his words and did not lightly override them.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong had already set the northern campaign in motion and would not halt it, though he did give serious weight to Hongjing's counsel.

sentences.zh: 弘靖知終不聽用，遂自陳乞罷政事。

translations.literal: Hongjing knew his advice would in the end not be heeded; he thereupon petitioned on his own behalf to leave political affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he would not be heeded, Hongjing asked to leave the government.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事，充太原節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly acting Minister of Personnel, associate director of the secretariat-chancellery, and installed as Taiyuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made acting minister of personnel and associate director of the secretariat-chancellery, with appointment as military governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 行未及鎮，果下詔誅承宗。

translations.literal: Before he had traveled to his command, an edict was indeed issued condemning Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post, the edict condemning Chengzong was issued as he had feared.

sentences.zh: 弘靖以驟諫不行，宜用自效，大閱軍實，請躬討承宗。

translations.literal: Hongjing, because urgent remonstrance had not been followed, wished to prove himself through action; he greatly reviewed military resources and asked to campaign personally against Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Since his urgent advice had been ignored, Hongjing sought to redeem himself, mustered his forces, and asked to lead the campaign against Chengzong in person.

sentences.zh: 詔許出軍，不許自往。

translations.literal: An edict permitted sending out troops but did not permit going in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor authorized him to dispatch troops but refused to let him go in person.

sentences.zh: 俄而魏博、澤潞悉為承宗所敗，有詔賞其前言。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Weibo and Zelu were all defeated by Chengzong; an edict rewarded Hongjing for his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the forces of Weibo and Zelu were defeated by Chengzong, and an edict commended Hongjing for his earlier counsel.

sentences.zh: 弘靖即間道發使懇喻承宗，承宗因亦款附。

translations.literal: Hongjing immediately sent envoys by a secret route to earnestly persuade Chengzong; Chengzong therefore also submitted in sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing then sent envoys by a back route to urge Chengzong to submit, and Chengzong did capitulate.

sentences.zh: 旋徵拜吏部尚書，遷檢校右僕射、宣武軍節度使，時韓弘入覲之後也。

translations.literal: Shortly summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel; transferred to acting Right Vice Director and Xuanwu Army military commissioner—this was after Han Hong entered court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as minister of personnel and appointed acting right vice director and military governor of the Xuanwu Army, after Han Hong had come to court.

sentences.zh: 弘靖用政寬緩，代弘之理。

translations.literal: Hongjing governed with lenient and relaxed policies, replacing Han Hong's administration.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing governed with a mild, unhurried hand, succeeding Han Hong.

sentences.zh: 俄以劉總累求歸闕，且請弘靖代己，制加檢校司空平章事，充幽州、盧龍等軍節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because Liu Zong repeatedly asked to return to court and also requested Hongjing replace him, an appointment added acting Grand Master of Works and chief minister, installed as military commissioner of Youzhou and the Lulong armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong repeatedly petitioned to return to court and asked that Hongjing replace him, Hongjing was appointed acting grand master of works and chief minister, and made military governor of Youzhou and the Lulong armies.

sentences.zh: 弘靖之入幽州也，薊人無老幼男女，皆夾道而觀焉。

translations.literal: When Hongjing entered Youzhou, the people of Ji—old and young, men and women—all lined the roads to watch.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjing entered Youzhou, the people of Ji, young and old, men and women, lined both sides of the road to watch.

sentences.zh: 河朔軍帥冒寒暑，多與士卒同，無張蓋安輿之別。

translations.literal: Military commanders in the Hebei region braved cold and heat; many shared conditions with soldiers, with no distinction of parasol and sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei generals usually shared hardship with their troops and did not ride under parasols in sedan chairs.

sentences.zh: 弘靖久富貴，又不知風土，入燕之時，肩輿於三軍之中，薊人頗駭之。

translations.literal: Hongjing had long been wealthy and noble, and moreover did not know local customs. When entering Yan, he was carried in a shoulder litter amid the three armies—the people of Ji were quite alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing, long accustomed to wealth and rank and unfamiliar with local ways, entered Yan carried in a sedan chair amid the army columns, which alarmed the people of Ji.

sentences.zh: 弘靖以祿山、思明之亂，始自幽州，欲於事初盡革其俗，乃發祿山墓，毀其棺柩，人尤失望。

translations.literal: Hongjing, because the rebellions of Lushan and Siming had begun from Youzhou, wished at the outset of affairs to thoroughly reform local custom; he therefore opened Lushan's tomb and destroyed the coffin—people were especially disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rebellions of An Lushan and Shi Siming had originated in Youzhou, Hongjing wanted to uproot the old ways from the start. He opened An Lushan's tomb and destroyed the coffin, which disappointed the people all the more.

sentences.zh: 從事有韋雍、張宗厚數輩，復輕肆嗜酒，常夜飲醉歸，燭火滿街，前後呵叱，薊人所不習之事。

translations.literal: Among his staff were Wei Yong, Zhang Zonghou, and several others who were again frivolous and fond of wine; they often returned drunk at night, torchlights filling the streets, escorts shouting before and behind—things the people of Ji were not accustomed to.
translations.idiomatic: Several of his staff, including Wei Yong and Zhang Zonghou, were arrogant and heavy drinkers. They often came home drunk at night with torches lighting the streets and attendants shouting ahead and behind—customs foreign to Ji.

sentences.zh: 又雍等詬責吏卒，多以反虜名之，謂軍士曰：「今天下無事，汝輩挽得兩石力弓，不如識一丁字。」

translations.literal: Moreover Yong and the others reviled and censured clerks and soldiers, often calling them by the name "rebel captives"; they said to the troops: "Now the realm is at peace—you who can draw a two-stone bow are not as good as knowing one ding character."
translations.idiomatic: Yong and his fellows also abused the clerks and soldiers, calling them rebel bandits. They told the troops, "The empire is at peace now. What good is drawing a two-stone bow if you cannot read a single character?

sentences.zh: 軍中以意氣自負，深恨之。

translations.literal: The army, proud of martial spirit, deeply hated this.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers, proud of their martial spirit, deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 劉總歸朝，以錢一百萬貫賜軍士，弘靖留二十萬貫充軍府雜用。

translations.literal: When Liu Zong returned to court, one million strings of cash were granted to reward the troops; Hongjing retained two hundred thousand strings for miscellaneous military government use.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong returned to court, one million strings of cash were granted to reward the troops, but Hongjing kept two hundred thousand for miscellaneous military expenses.

sentences.zh: 薊人不勝其憤，遂相率以叛，囚弘靖於薊門館，執韋雍、張宗厚輩數人，皆殺之。

translations.literal: The people of Ji could not bear their anger; they therefore rose in succession in rebellion, imprisoned Hongjing at the Jimen inn, seized Wei Yong, Zhang Zonghou, and several others—all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ji could endure no more. They rose in rebellion, imprisoned Hongjing at the Jimen inn, seized Wei Yong, Zhang Zonghou, and several others, and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 續有張徹者，自遠使回，軍人以其無過，不欲加害，將引置館中。

translations.literal: Thereafter there was Zhang Che, returning from a distant mission; the soldiers, because he had no fault, did not wish to harm him and were about to lead him to the inn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Che was returning from a distant mission. The mutineers, seeing no fault in him, meant to bring him safely to the inn.

sentences.zh: 徹不知其心，遂索弘靖所在，大罵軍人，亦為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Che did not know their intent; he therefore sought where Hongjing was and loudly cursed the soldiers—he too was killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Che did not understand their intentions. He demanded to know where Hongjing was and cursed the soldiers loudly. The mutineers killed him too.

sentences.zh: 明日，吏卒稍稍自悔，悉詣館，請弘靖為帥，願改心事之。

translations.literal: The next day, clerks and soldiers gradually regretted themselves; all went to the inn, asked Hongjing to be commander, and wished to change hearts and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the clerks and soldiers began to regret their actions. They all came to the inn, asked Hongjing to be their commander, and pledged to serve him faithfully.

sentences.zh: 凡三請，弘靖卒不對。

translations.literal: Three times in all they asked; Hongjing ultimately did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Three times they asked. Hongjing never answered.

sentences.zh: 軍人乃相謂曰：「相公無言，是不赦吾曹必矣，軍中豈可一日無帥！」

translations.literal: The soldiers then said to one another: "The minister is silent—this means he will not pardon us; the army surely cannot go a single day without a commander!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers said among themselves, "The minister's silence means he will never forgive us. An army cannot go a day without a leader!

sentences.zh: 遂取硃洄為兵馬留後。

translations.literal: They therefore took Zhu Hui as acting military commander.
translations.idiomatic: They then installed Zhu Hui as acting military commander.

sentences.zh: 朝廷既除洄子克融為幽州節度使，乃貶弘靖為撫州刺史。

translations.literal: Once the court had appointed Hui's son Kerong as Youzhou military commissioner, Hongjing was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the court appointed Zhu Kerong, Zhu Hui's son, military governor of Youzhou, Hongjing was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷太子賓客、少保、少師。

translations.literal: Before long, transferred to Guest of the Crown Prince, junior guardian, and junior preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he was transferred to the posts of guest of the crown prince, junior guardian, and junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年六月卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Changqing year 4 he died, age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of Changqing 4, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 元和初，王承宗阻兵，劉總父濟備陳征討之術，請身先之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era, Wang Chengzong blocked with arms; Liu Zong's father Ji fully set forth plans for the punitive campaign and asked to lead in person.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era, when Wang Chengzong was in revolt, Liu Zong's father Ji laid out a full plan for the campaign and volunteered to lead it himself.

sentences.zh: 及出軍，累拔城邑。

translations.literal: When the army marched out, they repeatedly captured cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army marched, it captured city after city.

sentences.zh: 總既繼父，願述先誌，且欲盡更河朔舊風。

translations.literal: Once Zong succeeded his father, he wished to fulfill his father's will and moreover wanted to thoroughly change the old ways of the Hebei region.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong succeeded his father, he wished to carry out his father's intentions and thoroughly reform the old ways of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，累表求入朝，兼請分割理之地，然後歸朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, he repeatedly memorialized asking to enter court, and moreover asked to divide the territory under his administration, then return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era he repeatedly petitioned to come to court, asking to divide the territory under his command before surrendering his post.

sentences.zh: 其意欲以幽、涿、營州一道，請弘靖理之；

translations.literal: His intent was to take You, Zhuo, and Ying prefectures as one circuit and ask Hongjing to administer it;
translations.idiomatic: He intended to set You, Zhuo, and Ying prefectures apart as one circuit under Hongjing;

sentences.zh: 瀛州為一道，盧士玫理之；

translations.literal: Ying Prefecture as one circuit, Lu Shimei to administer it;
translations.idiomatic: Ying Prefecture as another under Lu Shimei;

sentences.zh: 平、薊、媯、檀為一道，請薛平理之。

translations.literal: Ping, Ji, Gui, and Tan as one circuit, asking Xue Ping to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: and Ping, Ji, Gui, and Tan as a third under Xue Ping.

sentences.zh: 仍籍軍中宿將，盡薦於闕下，因望朝廷升獎，使幽、薊之人，皆有希美爵祿之意。

translations.literal: Moreover he registered veteran generals in the army and fully recommended them at court, thereby hoping the court would promote and reward them, so that the people of You and Ji would all have the desire for noble ranks and emoluments.
translations.idiomatic: He also listed the army's senior commanders for recommendation to the court, hoping that rewards and promotions would give the people of You and Ji reason to aspire to official rank and salary.

sentences.zh: 及疏上，穆宗且欲速得范陽，宰臣崔植、杜元穎又不為遠大經略，但欲重弘靖所授而省其事局。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Muzong moreover wished quickly to obtain Fanyang; chief ministers Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying did not pursue far-reaching strategy but only wished to weight what Hongjing was granted and reduce the administrative apparatus.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Emperor Muzong wanted to secure Fanyang quickly. Chief ministers Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying lacked a long-term strategy; they simply wanted to expand Hongjing's authority while simplifying the administrative structure.

sentences.zh: 唯瀛、莫兩州許置觀察使，其他郡縣悉命弘靖統之。

translations.literal: Only Ying and Mo two prefectures were permitted to establish observation commissioners; all other commanderies and counties were ordered entirely under Hongjing's unified command.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ying and Mo were allowed separate observation commissioners; all other prefectures and counties were placed under Hongjing's sole authority.

sentences.zh: 時總所薦將校俱在京師旅舍中，久而不問，硃克融輩僅至假衣丐食，日詣中書求官，不勝其困。

translations.literal: At that time all the generals and officers Zong had recommended were lodged in capital inns; for a long time no inquiry was made; Zhu Kerong and his fellows barely managed to borrow clothes and beg food, daily visiting the Secretariat to seek appointments, unable to bear their hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile every officer Liu Zong had recommended languished in capital lodgings with no word from the court; Zhu Kerong and his companions scraped by on borrowed clothes and alms, trudging daily to the Secretariat to beg for posts until they were at their wits' end.

sentences.zh: 及除弘靖，命悉還本軍。

translations.literal: When Hongjing was removed, an order was issued that all return to their original armies.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hongjing was dismissed, the court ordered them all sent back to their home commands.

sentences.zh: 克融輩雖得復歸，皆深懷觖望，其後因為叛亂。

translations.literal: Although Kerong and his fellows were able to return, they all harbored deep resentment, and afterward they rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong's party did return, but nursed bitter grievances and later broke into revolt.

sentences.zh: 初，總以平、薊、媯、檀請薛平，於分裂之中尤為上策，而朝廷不能行之，竟致後患，人到於今惜之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zong had requested that Ping, Ji, Gui, and Tan be given to Xue Ping—among schemes of partition this was especially the superior policy—but the court could not carry it out, and in the end later troubles arose; people to this day regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Zong had wanted Ping, Ji, Gui, and Tan placed under Xue Ping—the wisest cut in a partition plan—but the court never acted on it, inviting the troubles that followed; people still mourn the lost chance.

sentences.zh: 子文規、景初、嗣慶、次宗。

translations.literal: His sons were Wengui, Jingchu, Siqing, and Cizong.
translations.idiomatic: He left sons Wengui, Jingchu, Siqing, and Cizong.

sentences.zh: 文規，歷拾遺、補闕、吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Wengui served in turn as remonstrance official, collator, and external vacancy in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui rose through remonstrance officer, collator, and external vacancy in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 開成三年十一月，右丞韋溫彈劾文規：長慶中父弘靖陷在幽州，文規徘徊京師，不尋赴難，不宜塵汙南宮，乃出為安州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaicheng, Vice Director Wei Wen impeached Wengui: in the Changqing era his father Hongjing was trapped in Youzhou, yet Wengui lingered in the capital and did not hurry to his rescue—he ought not stain the southern palace; he was therefore sent out as Prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In November 838 Vice Director Wei Wen impeached Wengui: during Changqing his father Hongjing was trapped in Youzhou while Wengui idled in the capital instead of rushing to help—unfit, said Wen, to pollute the inner court—and Wengui was posted out as prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷右散騎常侍、兼御史中丞、桂管都防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and commissioner-over-all for defense and observation of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to right regular attendant of the cavalry, concurrent censor-in-chief, and commissioner-over-all for defense and observation in Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 景初，歷職使府，官止殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Jingchu served in commissioner offices; his highest post was Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu served in various commissioner staffs and rose no higher than palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 嗣慶，位終河南少尹。

translations.literal: Siqing's highest post was Vice Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Siqing ended his career as vice intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 次宗最有文學，稽古履行。

translations.literal: Cizong was most accomplished in letters and investigated antiquity in his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Cizong was the most learned, grounding his conduct in classical precedent.

sentences.zh: 開成中，為起居舍人。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era he was Attendance Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaicheng he served as attendance gentleman.

sentences.zh: 文宗復故事，每入閣，左右史執筆立於螭頭之下，宰相奏事，得以備錄。

translations.literal: Wenzong restored the old practice: whenever he entered the council hall, the left and right recorders stood brush in hand below the hornless dragon head; when chief counselors reported affairs, they could make full records.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong revived the old custom: on each entry to the council hall the left and right recorders stood with brushes below the hornless dragon frieze so they could capture everything the chief counselors reported.

sentences.zh: 宰臣既退，上召左右史更質證所奏是非，故開成政事，詳於史氏，次宗尤稱奉職。

translations.literal: After the counselors withdrew, the emperor summoned the left and right recorders to verify again whether what had been reported was right or wrong; therefore Kaicheng government affairs are detailed in the histories, and Cizong was especially praised for fulfilling his duty.
translations.idiomatic: After the counselors left, the emperor called the recorders back to verify their accounts, so Kaicheng politics are unusually full in the histories—and Cizong was singled out for dutiful service.

sentences.zh: 改禮部員外郎，以兄文規為韋溫不放入省出官，次宗堅辭省秩，改國子博士兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was changed to external vacancy in the Ministry of Rites; because his elder brother Wengui had been barred from entering the Secretariat by Wei Wen and sent out to office, Cizong firmly declined provincial rank and was changed to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, concurrently compiler at the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to external vacancy in the Ministry of Rites, he refused provincial rank when his brother Wengui was driven from the Secretariat by Wei Wen and took instead an erudite post at the Directorate of Education with a concurrent compiler's title at the History Office.

sentences.zh: 出為舒州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Shuzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as prefect of Shuzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 文規子彥遠，大中初由左補闕為尚書祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: Wengui's son Yanyuan, at the beginning of Dazhong, rose from Left Collator to external vacancy in the Secretariat's Shrine Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui's son Yanyuan, early in Dazhong, rose from left collator to external vacancy in the secretariat shrine office.

sentences.zh: 景初子天保，嗣慶子彥修，次宗子曼容。

translations.literal: Jingchu's son Tianbao, Siqing's son Yanxiu, Cizong's son Manrong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu left son Tianbao; Siqing left Yanxiu; Cizong left Manrong.

sentences.zh: 延賞東都舊第在思順裏，亭館之麗，甲於都城，子孫五代，無所加工，時號「三相張氏」云。

translations.literal: Yanshang's old eastern-capital mansion was in Sishun Lane; its pavilions and halls in beauty ranked first in the capital; for five generations descendants added nothing to it; at the time they were called "the Zhang family of three chancellors."
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang's old mansion in the eastern capital stood in Sishun Lane, its pavilions unrivaled in the city; five generations left it untouched, and the clan was known as "the Zhangs of three chancellors."

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：君民足則國富，將相和則國安，反是道焉非得人者。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When ruler and people are sufficient the state is rich; when generals and ministers are in harmony the state is secure—contrary to this way, how can one fail to lose the right men?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When ruler and people prosper, the state grows rich; when generals and ministers work in harmony, the state stays secure—turn that path upside down and you will surely lose the men the realm needs.

sentences.zh: 滉殺元琇，奏瑞鹽，逞斡運之能，非貞純之士，刻下罔上，以為己功。

translations.literal: Huang killed Yuan Xie, memorialized on auspicious salt, displayed his talent for transport management—he was not a man of pure integrity; he carved down those below and deceived those above, making it his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huang destroyed Yuan Xie, touted miraculous salt, and flaunted his transport empire—no upright man, but one who ground down subordinates, deceived superiors, and called it achievement.

sentences.zh: 幸逢多事之朝，例在姑息之地，幸而獲免，余無可稱。

translations.literal: Fortunately he met a court of many troubles, customarily in a place of indulgence; fortunately he escaped punishment—beyond that nothing is praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in turbulent times when indulgence was the rule and narrowly escaped ruin—nothing else worth praise.

sentences.zh: 延賞以私害公，罷李晟兵柄，使武臣不陳其力矣；

translations.literal: Yanshang harmed the public with private ends, removed Li Sheng's military authority, and caused military men not to offer their strength;
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang let private spite harm the public good, stripped Li Sheng of command, and left martial men unwilling to give their full strength;

sentences.zh: 惡直醜正，擠柳渾相位，致賢者不進其才矣。

translations.literal: he hated the upright and shamed the correct, squeezed Liu Hun from the chancellorship, and caused worthy men not to advance their talents.
translations.idiomatic: he hated the upright and drove Liu Hun from the chancellorship so worthy men could not bring their talents forward.

sentences.zh: 象恭僝功，皆四凶之跡也，雖以廕繼世，以才進身，蹈非道者，實小人哉！

translations.literal: Pretending respect while hoarding merit—all are traces of the Four Evils; although they inherited rank by yin privilege and advanced by talent, those who tread the unrighteous way are truly petty men!
translations.idiomatic: Outward deference masking selfish gain—the marks of the Four Evils; born to privilege and promoted for talent, yet walking unrighteous paths—they were small men indeed!

sentences.zh: 延賞歷典名籓，皆稱善政，及登大位，乃彰飾情。

translations.literal: Yanshang throughout governed famous circuits, all called good government; once he reached the highest rank, he then displayed ornamented feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang's terms in famous circuits won praise for good government; at the summit of power his true colors showed.

sentences.zh: 臯叠處大僚，徒稱舊德；

translations.literal: Gao repeatedly held great offices, only praised for old virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Gao piled up high offices while resting on old reputation alone;

sentences.zh: 弘靖輕傲邊事，欺減軍資；

translations.literal: Hongjing treated frontier affairs lightly and arrogantly, cheated and reduced military funds;
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing treated the frontier with contempt and shortchanged the troops;

sentences.zh: 洄附元載、楊炎，繼及累貶，俱非守正中立者也。

translations.literal: Hui attached to Yuan Zai and Yang Yan, and in succession suffered repeated demotions—all were not men who held to the center uprightly.
translations.idiomatic: Hui clung to Yuan Zai and Yang Yan and suffered repeated demotions—none of them stood upright at the center.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「世祿之家，鮮克由禮。」

translations.literal: The Documents says, "Families that inherit stipends seldom can follow ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "Houses that live on hereditary stipends seldom keep to ritual."

sentences.zh: 不其是歟！

translations.literal: Is this not so!
translations.idiomatic: Is that not exactly the case!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：韓滉刻下，延賞害公。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Han Huang carved down those below; Yanshang harmed the public good.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Han Huang ground down his subordinates; Yanshang injured the public good.

sentences.zh: 臯、洄繼世，弘靖興戎。

translations.literal: Gao and Hui inherited generations; Hongjing raised military troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Gao and Hui inherited rank; Hongjing stirred war.
